703	## Architecture Principles
704	
705	1. **The simulation is the truth, and it is pure data.** Every gameplay fact lives in a kernel-registered state block owned by exactly one system, built from `RefCounted` objects and packed arrays, with no `Node`, no `Resource` and no scene-tree dependency. It runs headless and is unit-testable. *(Pillar 1; TD-FEASIBILITY risk "graph entangled with the scene tree".)*
706	2. **Every change is a command, and the host is the authority, even in single-player.** Player intent enters only as a plain-data command stamped with its issuer; cross-system writes go only through the owner's published mutators inside a kernel WriteScope. Co-op is a transport added later, not a rewrite. *(TD-FEASIBILITY B2.)*
707	3. **Presentation reads, never writes; perception never reaches the simulation.** Presentation subscribes to change notifications and draws from read views. A hallucination is a presentation-side transform through `perceived()`; `PERCEPTION_OUT` is unreadable from the simulation, and truth channels (trails, real light radius, character sprites, crewmate beams, physical consequences) never pass through the Filter. *(Pillar 4 guard rails; "no lie is unfalsifiable".)*
708	4. **Deterministic by construction.** Fixed 60 Hz integer ticks, integer state, ascending-id iteration, keyed RNG streams with persisted counters, and one hash definition. Same save bytes plus the same restore epoch and command stream give the same state hash. Determinism is what makes replay tests, save verification and later co-op mirroring possible.
709	5. **Versioned, verified persistence from v1.** Saves serialise data models, never scenes; every block carries a schema version migrated by its owner; every file is self-verifying and written atomically; a bad save never faults the kernel and never overwrites a good one. *(TD-FEASIBILITY: "save format not versioned from v1".)*
710	6. **Budgets are measured, not assumed.** Every performance claim is a P99 on a Godot 4.7.2 release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK; hot paths allocate nothing per tick; work is bounded by construction (caps and counted work units, never wall-clock), so a budget miss is a tuning change, not a redesign.

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

content.content:
# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

**SL-1 — Container and header.** One file holds one **generation** (or, for the PROFILE store, one profile image — SL-9). Layout is the contract:

| Offset | Size | Field | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 8 | magic | A fixed 7-byte ASCII prefix followed by one byte, the container-layout id (1 for `FORMAT_VERSION` 1). The layout-id byte names the header/payload encoding only; it never locates the trailer (format law below) |
| 8 | 4 | `header_len` | Unsigned, little-endian; `0 < header_len ≤ MAX_HEADER_BYTES` and `12 + header_len + 32 ≤ file size`, checked **before any allocation** (a corrupt 4 GiB length is never allocated) |
| 12 | `header_len` | JSON header | UTF-8 object (fields below) |
| 12 + `header_len` | rest − 32 | payload region | The block payloads, concatenated in block-table order (SL-2) |
| end − 32 | 32 | trailer | SHA-256 of every preceding byte (magic through the last payload). It lives outside the header because a header cannot contain a hash of itself; a missing or short trailer is truncation, detected for free |

**Format law (every layout, forever).** For every file bearing the 7-byte magic prefix, in every container layout, the last 32 bytes are SHA-256 over all preceding bytes, `[0, size − 32)`. The layout-id byte names the header/payload encoding only. A reader can therefore verify integrity before it judges the layout id, so one flipped bit in the layout-id byte is reported as corruption (and falls back, SL-11) rather than as "made by a newer build" (which must not).

*(Orchestrator ruling: the trailer is additive to the layout in R1 — the file must be self-verifying (R3) and a header cannot hash itself. Payload region and file wrapper stay separable so the same payload can be sent to a guest at VS-B session start (CR-18) without the wrapper.)*

Header fields (closed list for format 1; unknown extra keys are ignored when `min_reader_version` is satisfied, missing required keys refuse, except `state_hash`, whose presence rules are in its row) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `format_version` | int ≥ 1 | Container version; `FORMAT_VERSION` 1 today |
| `min_reader_version` | int | Oldest reader that may open the file. In the MVP it equals `format_version` on every write (an older build can never read a newer file's blocks); the field exists so a later additive header change can lower it deliberately |
| `file_kind` | enum | `WORLD` (a generation) or `PROFILE` (SL-9) |
| `game_version`, `build_id` | string | File metadata written by the service; never read by the sim (H9) |
| `catalogue_version` | int | Item/module content epoch — the Item & Module Database's name (designed; IDB-26 `meta.json` key, IDB-27, its Save/Load row; history OQ-13). `catalogue_hash` (hex) is diagnostic only |
| `registry_epoch` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | hex u64 | A digest of the writing build's sorted (`block_id`, `schema_version`, `added_in_format`) triples over its `persist` blocks. It lets the reader tell "the registry moved" from corruption: a mandatory-set or schema failure on a file whose `registry_epoch` differs from ours is INCOMPATIBLE-dev, never CORRUPT and never quarantined (SL-11, SL-14, T-5) |
| `hash_algo` | int | Names the 64-bit hash the kernel used for `state_hash` and per-block hashes at capture (2 = H64, the ratified default: first 8 bytes of SHA-256 via `HashingContext`, read little-endian; the header hex form is little-endian too, F-10, R-17 / user ruling X13; 0 xxHash64 and 1 FNV-1a 64 are reserved ids, not written), so a later hash change needs no `format_version` bump (SL-16) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)* |
| `codec` | int | 0 = none; 1 reserved (zstd). No compression in the MVP (SL-19) |
| `tick_rate` | int | Must equal the kernel's `TICK_RATE`; a save is bound to the rate that wrote it |
| `T`, `world_seed` | hex u64 | Copied from `kernel.clock`; pre-check asserts they equal the block's values |
| `state_hash` | hex u64 | Kernel `state_hash(PERSIST, T)` of the WORLD blocks at capture (D.12, cited); absent in `PROFILE` files; written in every build, release included (K-4 adopted, kernel CR-15) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. A WORLD file whose `build_id` names a release build that predates K-4 loads without it with verdict `NONE` (the reproduction compare records no verdict); any other WORLD file without it is refused `SL_PRECHECK_HEADER_FIELD_MISSING` (AC-SL-100) |
| `campaign_id` | hex, 32 chars | 128-bit random; must equal the directory name |
| `generation` | int, < 2^53 | Strictly increasing per campaign; **the ordering truth** (SL-3) |
| `restore_epoch` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14)* | int, 0 ≤ v < 2^32 | A **read-only write-time copy** of the campaign's `restore_epoch` (SL-23) as it stood when this generation was written. It is never rewritten: no generation file is rewritten after `VERIFYING`, so the trailer SHA-256 and every key derived from the file stay fixed. The live value is in `slot_epoch.bin` (SL-19, SL-23 (0)); this copy is read only when `slot_epoch.bin` is missing or fails its CRC32 (SL-23 (2b)). A header int (never hex), `WORLD` files only (absent in `PROFILE` files). Missing, non-integral or ≥ 2^32 refuses (`SL_PRECHECK_HEADER_FIELD_MISSING` / `_TYPE` / `_NOT_INT`). It can reach the sim through the recovery rule, so it stays a behaviour-changing field and AC-SL-13 tags it MUST_REFUSE when damaged |
| `save_kind`, `trigger` | enum, string | `AUTO` / `EVENT` / `QUIT`; `trigger` names the event (names provisional until the registry merge: `POD_ARRIVED`; `ASSEMBLY_WELD` / `ASSEMBLY_CUT` are registered, SL-4); the initial generation is `EVENT` with trigger `NEW_GAME` |
| `risky` | bool | Written while a soft gate condition was closed, including a Save & Quit that bypassed one (SL-5, SL-6) |
| `risky_cause` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | string[] | The closed set of soft inputs that were true at the write: `GRAPH_TELL`, `ATTENTION_TELL`, `BREACH_PHASE`, `SEAT_STATE`, `VITALS`, `ASSEMBLY_BREACH`; empty exactly when `risky` is false. A member outside the set, or a non-empty list with `risky` false, is refused (`SL_PRECHECK_HEADER_FIELD_TYPE`). SL-8 reads it: a `QUIT` generation keeps the RISKY-window step-back only when `VITALS` is in it |
| `created_unix` | int | Wall clock, metadata only (SL-23) |
| `seats` | int[] | PlayerIds present, for validation only (SL-20) |
| `crew_count`, `depth_label` | int, string | `SaveInfo` inputs computed from SIM blocks at capture; `depth_label` (provisional — derived from the `ring` of the pod's node in `web.view`; Web Map & Transit publishes a ring, not a depth-label field) |
| `blocks[]` | records | `{block_id, schema_version, persist_scope, offset, length, payload_sha256 (64 hex), block_state_hash (hex, optional)}` per block; entries are contiguous, ascending, non-overlapping and sum exactly to the payload region |

**64-bit rule (S-1).** Every header value that can exceed 2^53 (`T`, `world_seed`, `state_hash`, per-block hashes, `campaign_id`) is an exact-width lowercase hex string (16 characters for 64-bit, 32 for 128-bit), never a JSON number; hex decoding is exact-width — a wrong length, uppercase or non-hex character is a refusal — and the contract is "8 bytes in, 8 bytes out" with no general string-to-int parse. Header numbers that stay numbers (`format_version`, `schema_version`, `generation`, lengths, offsets, counts, `hash_algo`, `codec`, `tick_rate`) arrive as floats from the parser (the Graph GDD's technical-director note, LS-21) and must be integral and below 2^53 before conversion. A `world_seed` ≥ 2^63 would read as a negative signed integer in GDScript [UNV]; it is stored as the hex of its 8 bytes. **File bytes are not canonical:** dictionary iteration is insertion-ordered (kernel D.12), so two saves of identical state can differ byte for byte. State equality is `state_hash` (or the owners' canonical bytes), never file bytes; the file SHA-256 guards *these bytes* against accidental damage; golden saves are immutable artefacts regenerated only deliberately.

**SL-2 — Interchange form and trust model (S-1, K OQ 7, D1).** Each block payload is the owner's `snapshot()` dictionary encoded with `var_to_bytes(dict)` (the form that does not encode objects) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (the earlier `allow_objects = false` argument is not a Godot 4 call shape; the object-allowing forms are the separate `var_to_bytes_with_objects` and `bytes_to_var_with_objects`, which are forbidden) [UNV], or the owner's own canonical byte form where it publishes one (the Graph's `canonical_bytes()`, LS-21), as raw bytes inside the container. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: Item DB IDB-16, registry `item_instance_to_array`, G1/G6)* A **value** embedded inside any holder block also takes its owner's published canonical form: an `ItemInstance` inside any block (today `suit.state` and `interaction.state`, and any future holder) is the Item DB's positional six-element array from `to_array()` = `[def_id, count, condition_bp, cap_bp, patched_at_step, charge]`, encoded as part of the block's `var_to_bytes`, and decoded only by `from_array(a, graph_step_no)` (registry `item_instance_to_array`, IDB-15). A Dictionary form of an instance is not an accepted encoding; this closes the open `var_to_bytes(dict)` route IDB-16 names. The reasons are one byte form per instance, a fixed schema and the size budget (the kernel's `canonical_bytes` already sorts dictionary keys, D.12, so this is not a `state_hash` fix). JSON appears **only** in the header. Decoding uses `bytes_to_var(bytes)` only, never `bytes_to_var_with_objects`; the object-allowing decode, `Resource` and `.tres` paths are forbidden outright (a script path can ride inside a resource; the Graph states "never a `Resource` for saves"). This is the answer to the kernel's Open Question 7. S-1 is carried verbatim: **64-bit integers cannot round-trip JSON text** (Godot's JSON parses numbers as float — the technical director's sourced note in LS-21), so no hashed, 64-bit or packed data ever travels as a JSON number; a payload that stored a packed array as a JSON number list is refused by the Graph's decoder (`GRAPH_RESTORE_BAD_TAG`). A dev-only `dump-save` command renders any block as JSON with 64-bit values as strings; it is diagnostics, never a load path. After decoding, a bounded walk (`MAX_DECODE_DEPTH`, `MAX_DECODE_NODES`; a packed array counts as one node) checks types before any `request_restore`, because `bytes_to_var` (the form without objects) stops object instantiation but does not by itself bound allocation or nesting [UNV]: allowed are null, bool, int, float, String, Array, Dictionary and the packed arrays (the H7 set, kernel CR-14); `Vector2i`, float vectors, `Color`, `Rect2`, `Object`, `Callable`, `Signal`, `RID`, `NodePath` and `StringName` are forbidden (kernel H7, K:125, enumerates no types: the allowed set is this GDD's reading of it, and K:839's JSON round trip cannot carry a `Vector2i`, which stringifies, so allowing it would make format 1 depend on K-3 landing); integer vectors travel as two ints or a packed int array (a shape note for the Body author — Ship Body & Interior Physics, designed, whose tables are integer-only (BDY-5); revisited only if K-3 changes K:839, OQ-9); dictionary keys are `String` or `int`; `snapshot()` uses untyped containers until the spike resolves typed-container encoding [UNV]. The kernel text that calls the interchange form "JSON-safe primitives" (CR-8) and its acceptance criterion that round-trips through J

**SL-3 — Generation ring.** `AUTOSAVE_GENERATIONS` 3 files (safe 2–5), each complete and self-verifying, at ring positions `gen_0.sav … gen_{N−1}.sav`. **Order is the header `generation` number — never the file name, the modification time or `T`** (after a step-back `T` rolls back while generation numbers keep rising; wall clock is untrusted). A new generation's number is `1 + max(generation seen in the ring, in `quarantine/` (read from the file name), among `.demoted` files and in the manifest)`. It is written into the first ring position that is free by F-9 (no `.sav` at all, or only a `.demoted`; an unreadable `.sav` occupies its slot) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* and is not claimed by an abandoned write job (SL-10) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; otherwise into the position of the **oldest** generation; the newest generation's file is never renamed or touched, so a window with no newest file cannot exist. *(Orchestrator ruling: R11 states the old newest is renamed to `.bak` during a swap; the three specialists converged on writing into the oldest position, where `.bak` holds the replaced oldest generation. R11's guarantee — never delete a generation before its successor verified — is kept and strengthened; the sequence is R11's "ADR candidate" and is stated in SL-10.)* To the player the ring is one logical autosave ("Continue"); it exists for corruption fallback and the RISKY rule (SL-8), not for choice, so the MVP API offers **no `load(generation)`** (a dev-build-only call may exist). `campaign.json` is a **hint, never truth**: a rebuildable cache of the ring (order, last write status, `suspect` counters); if missing or corrupt it is rebuilt by scanning generation headers and causes no refusal; the ring's truth is the set of generation headers and file names.

**SL-4 — Autosave triggers and manual save (D3).** Triggers: **interval** (`AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS` 10 800 = 3 min of sim time, safe 5 400–18 000 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, measured from `kernel.clock.T`), **events** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass)* (pod-hop arrival = Web Map & Transit's `POD_ARRIVED{tick, leg_epoch, at}` (`web_events`, provisional names until merge); weld or cut completion = Assembly's shape change, polled through the pure read `last_shape_change_T()` (MSA-33; event names `ASSEMBLY_WELD` / `ASSEMBLY_CUT` registered 2026-10-27, OQ-24); section extraction is Assembly's detach, served by the same `last_shape_change_T()`; a module cut is served by Interaction's pure read `last_salvage_T()` (registry `last_salvage_T`; IA-25; int64 tick or NONE; Boarding & Salvage BS-21), polled under SL-5's gate and `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS`; dock completion = Web Map & Transit's `BERTHED{tick, derelict_id}` (`web_events`, provisional until merge; `UNBERTHED` is not a trigger); an event trigger activates only when its owner publishes a notification or pure read Save/Load may consume), **Save & Quit** (SL-6) and the **initial generation** after `new_game` (SL-18). Events coalesce (kind only, never queued). **A RAGGED cut's `ASSEMBLY_CUT` event is withheld while Assembly's pure read `ragged_breach_open()` is true** (user ruling D54; the read is registered, source Modular Ship Assembly) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)*: the event stays latched, is not due, and is taken once the read turns false, that is until the keep-side cut room has vented (Assembly's read, band VACUUM) and its keep-side ports are capped or the port ceiling has passed *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; the `ASSEMBLY_WELD` event and a SEALED cut's `ASSEMBLY_CUT` are never withheld by it, and the open window also defers the interval save as a soft input (SL-5 row (d)) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* A minimum gap `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS` 1 800 separates any two interval/event generations; QUIT ignores it. An interval save is never due while the kernel is `PAUSED` (`T` cannot advance). The MVP set is interval + QUIT + initial + the `EVENT_TRIGGERS` set stated once in the MVP table and in Tuning Knobs (`ASSEMBLY_WELD`, `ASSEMBLY_CUT`, `SALVAGE_CUT` (registered) — the label for `last_salvage_T()` — and `POD_ARRIVED` / `BERTHED` once their names merge); an event whose owner read is absent never fires, and further events join as their owners land. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Shipping events at all trades a shorter typical loss against a learnable checkpoint grammar (the bonfire pattern this document rejects): the user confirmed that trade (Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): ship the weld, cut and module-cut event autosaves, D17, OQ-44) and metric M5 (Edge Cases) measures it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **Manual save is none in the MVP except Save & Quit** from the pause panel: save-anywhere is rejected because it makes every reload a free hallucination oracle (Pillar 4) and erases the cost of death (the user rule). A pinned main-menu-only manual slot is the single playtest fallback and is recorded in OQ-18, never an in-session save. The Chart Table's API (provisional) therefore has no `save_now()` in the MVP; if one ever appears it is marked "(provisional, reserved)" at every mention. The due-computation is Formula `autosave_due` (Formulas).

**SL-16 — Hash roles (D8; R10, R15).** Four distinct integrity layers, no overlap. (1) The **file trailer** SHA-256 over every preceding byte and (2) the per-block **`payload_sha256`** over each stored payload — Save/Load's own, fixed, native [UNV], verified before the kernel is touched; they localise damage and guard accidental corruption and truncation, not tampering. (3) The header **`state_hash`** and the optional per-block **`block_state_hash`** are the *kernel's* 64-bit hash over the owners' canonical bytes (D.12), named by `hash_algo`, so the ratified hash (H64 = first 8 bytes, little-endian, of SHA-256 via `HashingContext`, `hash_algo` 2; R-17, user ruling X13, registry `state_hash`) and the per-block cached hash (**K-1**, a kernel ADR candidate — cited, never owned) can change with no `format_version` bump *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)*; `block_state_hash` is present only if the kernel exposes a per-block hash, is diagnostic and is never a refusal reason. (4) The post-restore **reproduction compare** of SL-12 detects a restore that does not reproduce the snapshot — a bug, not corruption. The kernel's D.11 worked example assumed the hash cost is a debug-build cost; this design makes it a release cost on every capture and restore, and the ratified H64 is native, so the remaining cost question is whether SHA-256 over 100–300 KiB stays near the 1.5 ms that example allowed [UNV] — the spike (AC-SL-89) measures it, and K-1 is the mitigation if it does not (OQ-2, OQ-17) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Godot's `HashingContext` offers only MD5, SHA-1 and SHA-256 [UNV: 4.5 – 4.7 are post-cutoff, confirm in the spike], so a scripted `hash_algo` 0 (xxHash64) or 1 (FNV-1a 64) would be a per-byte loop, estimated at 15 to 150 ms over ~90 KiB (the range between the first review and the game-designer's estimate) [UNV]; a hitch that appears only on writes would tell the player when the game saved, the signal UI-1 was retired for. **Ratified** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)*: the default is the **native truncated SHA-256** (`hash_algo` 2, H64), which `HashingContext` computes natively (R-17, user ruling X13). With K-4 adopted (kernel CR-15) the capture-time `state_hash` has a release consumer and is written in every build (SL-1) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*.

**SL-17 — Zero blocks, zero hooks (D13).** Save/Load registers no state block and no step hook: ring bookkeeping lives in `campaign.json`, because a WORLD block would roll back on restore and desync the file set from the world. The kernel's acceptance criterion that the registry holds exactly one block, `kernel.clock`, stays true with Save/Load booted. Starting a new campaign over an existing one is destructive and defaults to retiring the old campaign (renaming it out of the active location); deletion is a separate explicit action under hold-to-confirm (HR-14, art bible; the UI is the Chart Table's). **No compression in the MVP** (typical size ≈ 100–300 KiB, kernel D.11 expectation); header `codec` 0 with 1 reserved; a size alarm at `SAVE_SIZE_ALARM_BYTES` 2 MiB (diagnostics only), re-evaluated at VS-A (600–1 200 Graph nodes). **Settings and key bindings are never in a snapshot**: Settings & Input Rebinding (Alpha) owns a per-client `ConfigFile`; Save/Load may expose only the atomic-write helper. A file whose `PER_PLAYER` keys are not a subset of `seats`, or whose `seats` is empty, duplicated or out of range, is refused (`SL_PRECHECK_SEATS_INVALID`). A Continue of any other generation (an `AUTO` or `EVENT` generation after a kill or crash, or an older generation reached by fallback) advances it. An advance sets `restore_epoch := min(2^32 − 1, max(e_mem, e_slot) + 1)`, `e_slot` the value last read from `slot_epoch.bin`; at 2^32 − 1 it saturates and logs. A step-back, a demotion, a quarantine or a lost manifest cannot lower it. A stub that finds nothing loadable (`SL_LOAD_NO_LOADABLE_SAVE`) restores nothing and does not advance it. (2) *Durable before the restore is requested (R14).* When an advance is due, Save/Load runs a pre-restore staging step: after selection, pre-check and staging (SL-8, SL-11) it computes the new value and hands the `slot_epoch.bin` write to the worker as its own job, never queued behind a generation write or an abandoned job (SL-10). ----
**SL-24 — Truth-only persistence (Pillars 1 and 4).** Save/Load never reads, derives, stores or varies by perception: no `PERCEPTION_OUT` block is ever written (a boot assertion and a pre-check step refuse one), no "what the player saw" field exists, no thumbnail, no sanity-dependent autosave timing, no hallucinated save list (H1, H6). the kernel's `LOADING` holds no wait on Save/Load I/O and stays atomic within one boundary service (kernel CR-15). *Staging interval (`t_epoch_wait`, F-8).* On the death stub the kernel stays `RUNNING` from the `DEAD` boundary to the boundary at which `request_restore` is made: normally one frame, at most `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (30 frames at 60 Hz). During it the seat stays `DEAD`, the hard gate is closed (a seat `DEAD`, a restore pending), and a `restore_pending` latch refuses every capture and pause request of Save/Load's (the dead world is never saved, SL-7) and answers further restore triggers with `SL_LOAD_REENTRANT`. The staged payload is immutable, so nothing ticked in the interval reaches the restored world except `PROFILE`-scoped writes (Pillar 5), and the Presenter holds the down sheet's last frame. For a Continue the staging runs behind the Continue press, before the kernel is touched; a carried Continue has no staging interval. (2a) *Failure path, a listed exposure.* If the write fails, or `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (placeholder 500, a monotonic I/O timeout) passes without `EPOCH_DURABLE`, Save/Load still calls `request_restore` with the advanced value held in memory, logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` and sets `save_status = FAILED`, because the device is failing and saving is impossible anyway. The worker re-attempts the `slot_epoch.bin` write with the next write job, and after every later `WRITTEN` generation Save/Load rewrites `slot_epoch.bin` whenever the in-memory value is ahead of the file. A kill before a later successful write may replay that epoch once (OQ-25). (2b) *Recovery copy.* A missing `slot_epoch.bin`, or one failing its CRC32, reads as `max(the newest verified generation's header copy, 0) + 1`, logs `SL_EPOCH_FILE_REBUILT` and is rewritten by the worker; a leftover `slot_epoch.tmp` is deleted (T-6). Deleting the side file by hand therefore re-keys the next stretch once, a tampering exposure of the same class as editing any save file (OQ-25). (3) *Reach into the sim.* `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash)` hands the value to the kernel, which exposes it read-only, sim-visible and pure in `kernel.clock` as `(T, world_seed, restore_epoch)` before the first `restore()`. The kernel owns the one derivation for threat draws, `counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE × restore_epoch` (`RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE` 1 048 576, owned by the kernel; the stream-name hash stays cached and unchanged); Attention and Horror call that derivation and define none of their own, and the name `threat_epoch()` is retired in favour of `restore_epoch`. The Graph's physical failures and every persisted counter never read it. (4) *Determinism is defined given the pair:* the same (save bytes, `restore_epoch`) replays identically, and tests pin the epoch (AC-SL-142, AC-SL-145). (5) *What it prices, stated plainly:* the player can neither pick nor predict the new value; a death re-keys the next stretch (the price, metric M2); a Save & Quit followed by Continue carries the epoch (R13), so the threat draws after it are those an uninterrupted run would meet and quit buys nothing (metric M3 measures only the disguised manual save); a kill then Continue of an `AUTO` or `EVENT` generation advances it, priced by the minutes lost since that autosave (OQ-25). A kill after a carried Continue, followed by a second Continue of the same `QUIT` generation, also carries the epoch and replays that stretch exactly, a repeat and not a re-key, an accepted exposure of the same kind as OQ-25's kill. History: the rule "advances on a death-stub restore only" and R1's rule "advances on every restore" are superseded by (1) (R13), and R1's header rewrite of the restored generation and its end-of-`LOADING` wait by (0) and (2) (R14). Save/Load stores true SIM state only (SL-24). Every interval, gap and window in SL-4, SL-5 and SL-8 is in ticks read from `kernel.clock.T`; `created_unix` and `game_version` are file metadata written by the service and never read by the sim (H9), so the tests are deterministic. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Wall clock, and the one exception.** The wall clock is never read in a decision about sim time. `SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS`, `RENAME_RETRY_DELAY_MS`, `READ_RETRY_DELAY_MS` and `DEATH_STUB_WRITE_WAIT_MS` are millisecond **I/O timeouts** that must run while `T` is frozen (`PAUSED`, `SAVING`, `LOADING`), so they read the engine's **monotonic** millisecond counter through an injected source; a timeout never changes sim state, schedules an autosave or enters a gate input. `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` is the fifth monotonic I/O timeout and the one that runs while `T` advances (the death stub's dead-world staging interval, (2)); it reads the same source and changes no sim state *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14)*. The Graph's note that "single-slot autosave is Save/Load's and the user's decision" is answered by SL-3's ring; the determinism argument is unaffected. The kernel's `rng_derive` note that a 63-bit owner-defined key is a valid `counter` appears only in OQ-3 as a routed kernel amendment (D.10), not as a rule here. A process kill after a mistake rewinds by at most one interval plus the deferral cap — the same price as dying, minus the death floor — and is an accepted, unpreventable exposure (no write can protect against it), recorded for playtest.
----SL10

Recovery on opening a campaign runs the crash-point scan of T-5: any `*.sav`, `*.bak` or `*.tmp` that verifies is accepted and ordered by `generation`; a file that cannot be proven obsolete is never deleted.

Temporary names carry `write_epoch` (`gen_<write_epoch>_<n>.tmp`), so an abandoned job's `.tmp` and a later job's can never be the same file. The worker re-reads `write_epoch` from its status record immediately before each ring-touching rename and aborts (removing its `.tmp`) if it is stale; a job that lands a generation despite that (the check-then-rename race, or a worker that resumed after being stuck past the check) reports its old `write_epoch`, and the main thread moves the file to `quarantine/` as `STALE_EPOCH`, never a candidate (SL-3). The worker is never killed. *Owner.* Capture and every `request_*` call stay on the main thread; the single Save/Load Node (SL-6, close mechanism) owns the worker handle and the poll. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Thread model, reaping, exit, lock.** *Model:* one `Thread` per job (no `WorkerThreadPool`), its handle held on a `RefCounted` `WriteJob` object that also carries the status record, so the thread's lifetime is the job's. *Reaping:* each poll (tick-boundary or frame) calls `wait_to_finish()` on a job whose thread reports `!is_alive()`; a job that is not alive and has published no terminal `WRITTEN` or `FAILED` status is a worker killed by a GDScript error: `SL_WRITE_WORKER_DIED`, `save_status` reads `FAILED`, `fail_n` is incremented, the ring position is released and the `.tmp` is left to T-6, instead of the 30 s `WRITE_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS` hold of the hard gate. *Cap:* at most `MAX_LIVE_ABANDONED_JOBS` (default 2) abandoned workers may be alive at once; at the cap a new write ends `FAILED` with `SL_WRITE_TOO_MANY_ABANDONED` and backs off until one reports. *Exit:* process exit never blocks on a busy or abandoned worker (no `wait_to_finish` on a live thread); a `QUIT` write that is itself busy follows SL-6's timeout, and an abandoned worker still running at exit is left to the OS, its `.tmp` handled by T-6 on the next open. *Single instance:* the campaign directory is opened under an exclusive lock (`campaign.lock`, created with an exclusive open and holding the process id; the mechanism and its behaviour under OneDrive and antivirus are [UNV], spike rows in AC-SL-30 and AC-SL-90); a second process that cannot take it opens the campaign **READ_ONLY**: it writes no generation, runs no T-6 deletion or quarantine move and offers New campaign and Quit only (AC-SL-147), because two processes would collide on `gen_` and `.tmp` names and T-6 would delete the other process's work.

136	### 6. The control plane is a host-local API on a `ControlHandle`
137	
138	`request_pause()`, `request_resume()`, `request_snapshot()`, `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash)`, `request_new_game(world_seed, restore_epoch)`, `request_shutdown()`, `request_bind_seat(peer_id, player_id)` and `request_unbind_seat(peer_id)` are methods of `ControlHandle`, not commands. They are not stamped, queued, authority-checked or logged as commands. Each call is appended to a small host-local request list and served **at the next boundary service, in arrival order** (ADR-0001 § 1), and each request ends in exactly one outcome: `SERVED`, `DEFERRED` (made while an atomic step was active; evaluated at the first boundary after it) or `IGNORED` (a (state, trigger) pair the transition table does not list; one invalid-transition entry, no state change). **Outcome delivery.** Outcomes are always recorded in diagnostics. Callers that must act on one set `ControlHandle.set_outcome_handler(Callable)` and receive a typed `ControlOutcome` (`request_kind`, `outcome`, `tick`, and for `request_restore` the K-4 verdict `{T, computed_hash, match}`; for `request_snapshot` the captured payload, a deep copy) at the same per-frame flush point as command results, **in a separate list that is never part of the CR-5 command result buffer**. This amends one sentence of the kernel GDD (States and Transitions, "control-plane requests have none"; § GDD sync): the outcome list is not a command result record, but it exists, because Save/Load needs the snapshot payload and the K-4 verdict (CR-15) and PauseGate needs to converge. Two consequences are intentional: a `request_pause` and a `request_resume` in the same boundary pair up in order, and `PauseGate` (Chart Table) re-issues the latest desired pause state until the kernel matches it, so a same-boundary pair leaves no wedged half-open state (TR-charttable-004).
139	
140	**Seat binding (binding table half (a)).** `request_bind_seat(peer_id, player_id)` and `request_unbind_seat(peer_id)` are the host-only writers of `peer_id → PlayerId` (CR-7). The composition root, holding the `game` control handle, calls `request_bind_seat(HOST_PEER_ID, 1)` as its boot step; the Co-op Session calls the same two methods in VS-B, so the kernel's public API does not widen then. A restore, new game or death restart never touches half (a). Runtime seat reassignment (kernel open question 4) is deferred to ADR-0032 under this signature. When `issuer_peer` has no half (a) entry, a type with `actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER` is `Rejected(ACTOR_NOT_OWNED)`; a `NONE` type proceeds.

### 6. Fault codes: static domains, pre-packed constants

A fault code is a positive `int`: `(DOMAIN_ID << 16) | local`, `local` in `1..65535`. **Domain ids are static**, so a code means the same thing in every build, log and fixture. Each system's `*_faults.gd` (a `class_name XFaults extends RefCounted` holding only constants, never instantiated, one class per file) declares `const DOMAIN_ID` and its codes **already packed** (`const NOT_IN_SCOPE: int = (DOMAIN_ID << 16) | 1`), plus `const NAMES: Array[StringName]` indexed by local code. It registers with `register_fault_domain(XFaults.DOMAIN_ID, owner_name, XFaults.NAMES)`; a duplicate or out-of-range id fails boot. A unit test checks each file's constants and `NAMES` agree. Codes are append-only and never reused. The kernel prints a fault as `domain.NAME`.

**Domain table** (static; new systems take the next free id; ids 32 and up are reserved for VS and later)

| Id | Domain | Id | Domain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | kernel | 8 | interaction |
| 1 | save_load | 9 | suit |
| 2 | content data (item DB, templates, tuning) | 10 | assembly |
| 3 | graph | 11 | web_transit |
| 4 | layout | 12 | attention |
| 5 | body | 13 | horror |
| 6 | emitter | 14 | sanity |
| 7 | controller | 15–31 | presentation and tooling (read-view faults are diagnostics only) |

**Kernel fault codes (domain 0, closed)**

| Local | Name | Raised when |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `INCOMPLETE` | a kernel-invoked callable did not return the armed token |
| 2 | `NO_OUTCOME` | `validate` called neither `ok()` nor `reject()` |
| 3 | `BINDING_REBUILD_CONFLICT` | the `LOADING` binding rebuild found a conflict or a binding-source fault |
| 4 | `RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BLOCK` | a restore payload names an unregistered block |
| 5 | `TICK_RATE_MISMATCH` | a payload was saved at another `TICK_RATE` |
| 6 | `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE` | the supplied `restore_epoch` is out of range |
| 7 | `CAPTURE_ERROR` | a `SAVING` capture failed |
| 8 | `DUPLICATE_ID` | boot: duplicate block, command, hook, domain or channel id |
| 9 | `HOOK_CYCLE` | boot: a cycle in hook `after` edges |
| 10 | `UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY` | boot: unknown `after` hook, `restore_after` block or `writes_blocks` block |
| 11 | `ACTOR_SOURCE_INVALID` | boot: a command type's `actor_source` rule fails (CR-6) |
| 12 | `COALESCE_DUAL_ORIGIN` | boot: a coalescing type allows both origins |
| 13 | `DESCRIPTOR_FIELD_MISSING` | boot: a mandatory descriptor field is absent |
| 14 | `SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TOO_LONG` | boot: `lcm` of divisors exceeds `MAX_SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TICKS` |
| 15 | `HOOK_OFFSET_INVALID` | boot: `divisor < 1` or `offset` not in `0..divisor-1` |
| 16 | `CALLABLE_SIGNATURE` | boot: a `Callable` is invalid or has the wrong arity |
| 17 | `MEMORY_BUDGET` | boot: the CR-17 joint memory assertion fails |

A P3 above `STEP_BUDGET_MS` is a **diagnostic** (it logs the slowest hooks), not a fault.

**Violations** are counted diagnostics, not fault codes, and never change kernel state unless the GDD says so. Closed set: `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE`, `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED`, `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE`, `CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME`, `CONTEXT_REENTRY`, `SUBMIT_DURING_SAVING`, `HANDLE_UNREGISTERED`, `RESULT_HANDLER_DEAD`, `DEAD_SUBSCRIBER`, `TIME_SCALE_NON_UNIT`, `KNOB_REFUSED`, `BINDING_DRIFT`, `WRITES_BLOCKS_UNDECLARED`, `STALE_EDGE_UNDECLARED` (a boot warning). Under `STRICT_DEBUG` each also calls `violation_handler(code, detail)`.

### 9. The kernel state machine is a data table

States: `BOOTING`, `LOADING`, `RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, `SAVING`, `FAULTED`, `SHUTTING_DOWN`. The GDD's transition table is encoded as one constant table `(state, trigger) → target`, where a target may be the sentinel **`PRIOR`** (`SAVING` returns to the state it came from).

- **Triggers** (closed): `request_pause`, `request_resume`, `request_snapshot`, `request_restore`, `request_new_game`, `request_shutdown`, `fault`, `capture_done`, `capture_error`, `load_done`, `load_failed`, `boot_validation_failed`, `teardown_done`.
- **Boot validation is not a trigger.** It is an internal step of the boundary that serves the first `request_new_game` / `request_restore` in `BOOTING`: on success the request proceeds (`BOOTING → LOADING` via the request's row); on failure the same boundary fires `boot_validation_failed` (`BOOTING → FAULTED`).
- **Deferral comes before the lookup.** A request made while an atomic step (`SAVING`, `LOADING`) is active is `DEFERRED` and evaluated, in arrival order, at the first boundary after the step, against the state that boundary finds. Only then is the table consulted; a pair not in the table is `IGNORED` with one invalid-transition diagnostics entry and no state change.
- **Seat binding is outside the table.** `request_bind_seat` / `request_unbind_seat` (ADR-0002) are non-transition requests: served at the boundary in `BOOTING`, `RUNNING` and `PAUSED` (`SERVED`), deferred during an atomic step, and `IGNORED` in `FAULTED` and `SHUTTING_DOWN`. They never change state.
- **Re-entry from `FAULTED` (closes OQ-5).** The kernel keeps `registry_valid: bool`, set true only by a passing validation pass. The `FAULTED` rows for `request_restore` and `request_new_game` apply only when `registry_valid`; a boot-failure `FAULTED` exits only through `request_shutdown`. A runtime fault keeps all three exits.

The control-plane test KRN-STATE-01 is **generated from this table**: every row, every invalid pair, both kinds of `FAULTED`, and the non-transition requests, so a row added without a fixture row fails.

### 10. Kernel members (the H1 allow-list)

Everything this ADR adds to the kernel lives under the GDD's allow-listed groups, so the H1 lint stays a fixed list: **registries** (descriptors, the compiled schedule, the fault-domain table, `registry_valid`, the transition table); **kernel_state** (current state, the `PRIOR` return state, the reused contexts, tokens and scope objects); **diagnostics** (violation counters, boot warnings, the fault log).

Proposed

2026-10-28

## Last Verified

## Summary
Sixty-five requirements from fifteen GDDs need static authored data (items, section templates, world records, tuning tables, lint configuration) to load identically in the editor, headless tests and a release export, to reach the simulation only as integers, and to keep ids stable across saves. This ADR fixes one pipeline: integer-only JSON under `assets/data/` listed in committed manifests (never a directory scan), read through an injected `ContentSource`, parsed with `JSON.new().parse`, cast through closed per-table schemas into write-once typed `RefCounted` catalogs, validated by one flat domain-2 boot-error list plus an offline lint that reuses the same loaders, and keyed by append-only id ledgers that CI diffs against a base revision.

## Context

### Problem Statement
Twenty-six GDDs make gameplay values, templates, catalogues and id spaces data-driven. Each GDD solved the same four problems locally and deferred the shared answer to this ADR: (1) the engine's JSON parser returns floats, but the simulation is integer-only; (2) a directory scan or an unlisted file can pass in the editor and fail or reorder in a release export; (3) a catalogue read by `validate`, P3 and presentation must be immutable, scene-tree free and allocation-free on lookup; (4) ids that reach a save, a snapshot or a hash must never change meaning. Without one decision, the Item DB, Layout, Graph, Derelict Authoring, Horror, Sanity and Audio would each ship a slightly different loader, and the first exported build would find the differences.

### Constraints
- **Integer-only simulation** (kernel, Graph LS-1, Layout LY-2). A float never reaches a sim read; designer floats convert once, at load.
- **No directory scan, no unordered iteration** (LY-2, IDB-4, LSG 64). The sim never iterates a `Dictionary`.
- **Same boot assertions in editor and export** (TR-sanity-026, AC-SN-178).
- **No autoload, static variable or group lookup** exposes content (registry `kernel_autoload_or_global`, ADR-0001); many catalogues coexist in one process (TR-itemdb-002).
- **Catalogs are never `Resource`** (registry `block_as_resource_or_node` extended by the same reasoning; SL-2; IDB-26 i).
- **No `assert`, no `push_error`, no `quit` in a loader** (`assert` is stripped in release; `push_error` trips gdUnit4; a loader that quits cannot be tested).
- **No `res://` path on any field that can reach a save** (IDB-26).
- **Unit tests do no file I/O** (coding standards): the loader needs a file-access seam.
- **Fault codes** follow ADR-0003 § 6: `(DOMAIN_ID << 16) | local`, one `*_faults.gd` per domain, `NAMES` indexed by local code, append-only.
- **Dependency direction** (architecture "Which way dependencies may point"): Foundation code under `src/data/` must not import `src/sim/`; no `preload` of a sibling system's script.
- **Load budget:** `ItemCatalog` load plus freeze creates exactly 25 Objects and P99 <= 14.9 ms desktop / 30.0 ms Deck, pending spike (TR-itemdb-024).
- **Pre-release saves are disposable** (LSG 832); ids become binding at the first build given to anyone outside the project.

### Requirements
- One `ContentLoader` path for every static table, used unchanged by the game, gdUnit4 fixtures and the offline lint.
- A closed schema per table; unknown key, missing key, wrong type, float where an integer is required, and out-of-range value are errors with a stable code.
- A committed manifest per content domain; load order is the manifest's order, itself required to be sorted.

content.content:
### 3. Stable ids, ledgers and versioning

**3.1 The rule.** An id that reaches a save, a snapshot, a hash, a replicated record or a `SalvageRecord` is one of three things only:
1. a **stable string key** chosen by a human (`def_id`, `template_id`, `room_key`, `derelict_id`);
2. an **integer in an append-only ledger** (§ 3.2);
3. a **Graph type-table id** (loop, node kind, port type, edge kind, mode, state), fixed by code constants (§ 3.2).

It is never an array index, a file or manifest position, a `Dictionary` iteration position, a hash of a path, or a `ResourceUID`. **Item `type_id` specifically never reaches a save, snapshot or hash** (IDB-3: it stays in memory and in vertical-slice replication summaries only); persisted item records carry `def_id`.

**3.2 Ledgers and code-fixed tables.**

*Ledgers.* An id space whose keys are persisted or hashed and that content authors extend has a committed `ids.lock.json`: `{ "space": "item_defs", "format": 1, "state": "PRE_RELEASE", "pairs": [ { "key": "mod_o2_tank", "id": 1001, "dormant": false } ], "retired_ids": [ 1002 ] }`. Required for the MVP: `item_defs` (IDB-4, `assets/data/items/ids.lock.json`) and `section_templates` (`template_id` and each template's `room_key`s, `assets/data/sections/ids.lock.json`, ADR-LAY-04; nesting per OQ-B). Other spaces (horror `type_id`, sanity surface enums, instrument ids, audio tokens) are unique- and range-checked at boot and gain a ledger when they first reach a save or hash.

*Boot check.* The generic `LedgerCheck.verify(live_pairs, ledger)` refuses with `CONTENT_LEDGER` (named `ITEM_BOOT_TYPE_ID(class, id)` for the Item DB) when:
- two live entries share an id;
- an id lies outside its space's declared range;
- a key's prefix disagrees with its class;
- an id is in `retired_ids`;
- a shipped key appears with a different id;
- a ledger pair is missing from live content without `dormant` or a `retired_ids` entry.

A **dormant** pair is cut from the current build but may return unchanged; no other key may take its key or id. A **retired** id is never reused.

*Code-fixed Graph tables.* The Graph's type tables are fixed enumerations whose **baseline is the code-side enum constants** owned by the Graph (ADR-0011). Boot checks that `assets/data/graph/` equals those constants exactly, refusing a duplicate, a missing entry or a renumber with `GRAPH_BOOT_TYPE_ID(table, id)`. A renumber therefore needs a reviewed code change, and ADR-0011 owns their stability; they need no ledger.

*CI append-only gate (`LEDGER_NOT_APPEND_ONLY`).* CI compares each ledger with the base revision (§ 2.2):
- pairs are only added;
- an existing pair's key or id never changes;
- `retired_ids` only grows;
- `dormant` may flip either way.

While `state` is `PRE_RELEASE` the gate reports WARN, because pre-release saves are disposable. The commit that sets `state` to `SHIPPED`, made when the first build leaves the project, is one-way and turns the gate into an ERROR.

**3.3 Renames and removals** (IDB-27). The format reserves `renamed_from[]` and `replaced_by` on defs now. Their behaviour is needed only after `SHIPPED`: transitive resolution to `ALIAS_DEPTH_MAX` 8 at restore through `resolve_alias`, and `ITEM_BOOT_ALIAS` on a cycle, a self-alias or an alias equal to a live key. It is implemented in a story that is a **prerequisite of the `SHIPPED` flip**, not in the MVP epic. A removed def that names no `replaced_by` fails restore loudly with the holder's named failure (`GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF` for Graph nodes).

**3.4 Versioning.** `catalogue_version` is a single integer in `meta.json`:
- It is bumped on any def removal, rename or field-shape change.
- It is **not** bumped for a value tuned within its type (F-9).

`VERSION_BUMP_MISSING` compares the catalog's structural signature (keys, field set, removed or renamed defs) with the base revision. It is WARN while the ledger is `PRE_RELEASE` and ERROR after `SHIPPED`. This ADR offers the integer to Save/Load's header, and ADR-0006 places it.

`catalogue_hash` is **diagnostic only and never gates a load**. It is `H64` over the canonical bytes of the post-cast typed rows, sorted ascending by `def_id` (byte order), so a legal renumber never changes it. The encoding and `H64` are ADR-0005's. This ADR fixes the *input*: typed integers after cast, never file bytes, never key order, never float spelling.

**3.5 Template identity and hashes.** `template_id` and `room_key` are stable keys under the `section_templates` ledger. `geometry_hash`, `visual_hash` and `template_hash` are `H64` of the canonical encoding of the post-cast template (ADR-0005). They are computed once at load and never stored in the template file. A template edit between builds is handled by Layout's drift policy (LY-26 e). Changing one authored value by 1 changes `template_hash` and `state_hash` (TR-derelict-007).

## Migration Plan
No code exists. **GDD sync applied 2026-10-28** (each edit is marked *Amended 2026-10-28 — ADR-0007 sync* in its GDD). The copies of TR-lsg-030 and TR-section-003 in `tr-registry.yaml` and `requirements-traceability.md` are refreshed by `/architecture-review` Phase 8, which owns those files. The edits were:
- `item-and-module-database.md`:
  - IDB-26: close the export-filter and `catalogue_hash` ADR candidates; adopt the `BootError` shape and the Item DB manifest.
  - IDB-30: the composition root acts, not kernel BOOTING; codes are domain 2.
  - IDB-27: alias behaviour is a pre-`SHIPPED` story.
- `ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md` LY-2 and LY-30: filter syntax; a template ledger; structural-lint codes are domain 2; "loaded in BOOTING" means start-up before the kernel.
- `life-support-graph.md`: the type-table baseline is the code enums; the `GRAPH_BOOT_TYPE_ID` code moves to domain 2 (`GRAPH_RESTORE_*` stays in domain 3).
- `sanity-and-hallucination-rules.md`: `SANITY_BOOT_LIE_TARGET_DATA` is domain 2.
- `suit-and-equipment.md`: ADR candidate 2 is closed (JSON).
- `failure-and-trail-system.md` and `emitter-state-and-light-exposure-query.md`: IC-12 wording.
- `architecture.md`:
  - § 8: static type tables load first; `graph.state` registers last.
  - Add CONTENT-EXP-1 to § Spikes that gate ADRs.
- `docs/architecture/tr-baseline.md`: rewording of TR-lsg-030 and TR-section-003 ("loaded in BOOTING"). Re-tagging of the owner-elsewhere rows above happens at `/architecture-review`.

## Validation Criteria
- CONTENT-EXP-1 passes on Windows and Linux/Deck: an exported `template_release` boots headless to `RUNNING` and its content hashes equal the editor's.
- A unit test per loader rule: each pipeline-generic code is raised by a `MemoryContentSource` fixture with exactly one defect; a defect-free fixture loads clean; a fixture with defects in two files of one stage reports both.
- Two `ItemCatalog` instances built in one process share no state.
- **Zero allocation is tested two ways**, because `OBJECT_COUNT` counts only Objects and misses arrays:
  - (a) `OBJECT_COUNT` is unchanged over 10,000 queries;
  - (b) two calls to each array-returning accessor return the same array (`is_same`), and `is_read_only()` is true.
- The 25-Object load check runs after every loader temporary is out of scope.
- A CI job fails on:
  - an unlisted `.json`;
  - a case mismatch;
  - an include-filter miss;
  - a raw-text shape or duplicate-key violation;
  - a non-append-only ledger change or a missing `catalogue_version` bump after `SHIPPED`;
  - a generated file that drifts from its generator;
  - any `DirAccess`, `FileAccess`, `JSON.parse_string` or `JSON.new` use for content outside `src/data/` (the lint is ADR-0010's).
- **After ADR-0005 is Accepted** (it depends on ADR-0005): golden `catalogue_hash` and per-template hash vectors are committed and change only with the encoding.

## Related
- Depends on: ADR-0001, ADR-0003 (both Proposed).
- Forward references: ADR-0005 (canonical encoding, `H64`), ADR-0006 (save header carries `catalogue_version`), ADR-0010 (lint tool, source layout, shared pure functions), ADR-0011 (Graph type enums), ADR-0013 (layout block), ADR-0016 (restore ordering), ADR-0030 (boot-failure surface styling).
- GDDs: `item-and-module-database.md` (IDB-3, 4, 26, 27, 30), `ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md` (LY-2, LY-30), `life-support-graph.md` (LS-2 to LS-5, ADR-LSG-08), `derelict-authoring-handmade-kits.md` (DA-4, DA-41, DA-43), `save-load-and-versioned-format.md`.
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md` § 8, § Required ADRs, § Spikes that gate ADRs, Open Question OQ-9.
- `docs/registry/architecture.yaml`: entries proposed by this ADR (state, interface, API decisions, forbidden patterns).

## Open Questions
- **OQ-A.** The composition root alone acts on content boot errors (content precedes the kernel), and domain 2 is not registered with the kernel at MVP. Revisit with ADR-0003 if the kernel GDD's boot-failure screen must be kernel-owned, or if a runtime path starts raising domain-2 codes.
- **OQ-B.** Whether the `section_templates` ledger holds one entry per `room_key` or one per template with a nested list (ADR-LAY-04 detail). This ADR requires the ledger and leaves the nesting to Layout's schema.

## Review Log
- **2026-10-28 godot-specialist (engine).** Idiomatic for 4.7.2; no removed or deprecated API.
  - Blocking, all applied:
    - B1: `const Array[FieldSpec]` does not compile; now `const` literal rows plus `static func fields()`.
    - B2: packed arrays are passed by reference and cannot be read-only; now typed read-only `Array[T]` or index accessors.
    - B3: `OBJECT_COUNT` misses arrays; identity and `is_read_only` checks added.
  - Minor, applied:
    - `set` renamed to `content`.
    - The `get_file_as_string` rationale is corrected.
    - Explicit BOM check.
    - `JSON_DUP_KEY` lint.
    - The 2^53 bound is now exclusive.
    - `MANIFEST_PATH_CASE` and a Linux leg.
    - LF `.gitattributes`.

Since the documentation is thin on Core file I/O behavior, I should probe the actual engine implementation instead—specifically how DirAccess.rename behaves on Windows when overwriting an existing file, checking whether the implementation handles replacement explicitly.

I'm also thinking through other engine facts worth verifying: locked file handling when renaming an open FileAccess writer, Thread lifecycle methods, store_buffer's return value, Marshalls/var_to_bytes serialization semantics, and whether GDScript has any built-in CRC32 support or if I'd need to implement it manually for a 4-byte checksum.

I'm now planning a set of probes to run in a scratch directory, starting with testing how DirAccess.rename behaves when overwriting an existing file on Windows, especially when that target file is locked by another open handle.

Beyond that, I'm listing further probes to check: FileAccess.store_buffer's return value and error state after flushing; whether var_to_bytes/bytes_to_var round-trips correctly for large int64 values and Vector2i, and what happens when bytes encoded with objects are decoded without that flag; how JSON.parse handles integers beyond float precision; whether Marshalls has a raw-to-base64 helper; and timing SHA256 hashing over a 300KiB buffer using HashingContext to get a sense of header overhead.

I also want to test Thread behavior (starting with a Callable, checking is_alive, wait_to_finish, and quitting mid-task), measure FileAccess write/flush/rename timing, and estimate the real-world hitch from var_to_bytes-ing a 300KiB snapshot plus hashing it. Beyond that, I need to investigate Windows file-sharing semantics -- whether a file opened for writing in one handle blocks reads, renames, or deletes from another handle -- along with DirAccess directory operations under user://, confirming FileAccess.get_sha256 exists, and acknowledging I can't directly verify whether flush() triggers an fsync.

Given the engine specifics are still unverified, I'm thinking I should write a quick probe script to test these things directly rather than keep speculating, then check in with the advisor before doing the real implementation work.

I'm discovering that FileAccess.open with WRITE mode actually truncates the file rather than providing exclusive access, so a second instance opening the same lock file succeeds and overwrites it—meaning exclusive-open-based locking isn't achievable with FileAccess alone on Windows, and I need to find another locking mechanism.

Instead, I'm considering holding a READ handle open to prevent rename/delete on Windows (though this doesn't work the same on Linux), or better, using a pid-based lock file: write the process ID into the lock file, then have a second instance check `OS.is_process_running(pid)` to detect if the original process is still alive, accepting a small race window as a tradeoff.

But I realize `OS.is_process_running` in Godot only tracks child processes spawned via create_process/execute, not arbitrary foreign PIDs -- so it's unreliable for checking another independently-launched instance. This is a fundamental limitation I need to flag as a spike item with weaker guarantees than I'd like.

| `NEWEST` | Highest `generation` among non-discarded files | Swap complete and manifest rewritten | A successor reaches `NEWEST` | → `OLDER`; → `DEMOTED`; → `QUARANTINED` | Writer; SL-8; the load pipeline | `gen_k.sav` |
| `OLDER` | A ring member below the newest | A successor became newest | Chosen as the position for reuse, demoted or quarantined | → overwritten by a successor; → `DEMOTED`; → `QUARANTINED` | Writer; SL-8; the load pipeline | `gen_k.sav` |

| `BAK` | The replaced oldest file during a swap | The position's file is renamed to `.bak` | Manifest verified, then removed; or promoted back on a failed swap | → removed; → `gen_k.sav` | Writer; boot recovery | `gen_k.bak` |
| `QUARANTINED` | Failed as CORRUPT, failed owner restore `QUARANTINE_AFTER_FAILURES` times, or landed `STALE_EPOCH` | The pre-check, the kernel or the `write_epoch` rule names it | Never leaves automatically | — | Load pipeline; epoch rule | `quarantine/…` with a reason |
| `SUSPECT` | Passed the file stage but failed the reproduction stage (`SL_VERIFY_NOT_REPRODUCED`) | Verification | A later generation reproduces (counter reset) | stays in the ring (release plays on; dev/test halts on the first occurrence); counter only, and `SUSPECT_THRESHOLD` is a diagnostics escalation | Verification (SL-12) | unchanged; counter in `campaign.json` |

**T-4. Write-procedure states.** A failure at any state leaves every previous generation exactly as it was. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Temporary names carry `write_epoch`: read every `gen_k.tmp` below as `gen_<write_epoch>_<k>.tmp` (SL-10), and the recovery scan of T-6 matches that pattern.

| State | `save_status` | Work (runs where) | Failure outcome on disk |
|---|---|---|---|
| `IDLE` | `IDLE` (or sticky `WRITTEN`/`FAILED`) | none | n/a |
| `CAPTURING` | `WRITING` | Kernel `SAVING`, synchronous snapshot; split by `persist_scope`; `SaveInfo` computed; per-block `var_to_bytes` only (main thread, tick halted); the **worker** hashes each block, builds the header (`payload_sha256`, `block_state_hash`), assembles header, payload region and trailer, and returns the complete image, which becomes the hot copy after `WRITTEN` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | A capture error takes the kernel to `FAULTED`; no file touched |
| `WRITING_TMP` | `WRITING` | Worker writes `gen_k.tmp`; **every `store_*` return is checked**; flush; close | Any false return or open error: `.tmp` removed best-effort, `FAILED` |

| `SWAPPING_OUT` | `WRITING` | If the position holds a file — the oldest generation, or a `.demoted` occupant, which is treated exactly like an oldest occupant — rename it to `.bak` (a stale verified `.bak` is deleted first; an unverified one aborts the write, `SL_WRITE_STALE_BAK`); the `.bak` is deleted after `POST_VERIFY` | Rename failure (retry `RENAME_RETRY_COUNT`): `FAILED`, the position's file still in place |
| `SWAPPING_IN` | `WRITING` | Rename `.tmp` → `gen_k.sav` (the target is absent, so no rename-onto-existing; Windows overwrite semantics are never relied on [UNV]) | Failure: roll back by renaming `.bak` back; `FAILED` |
| `POST_VERIFY` | `WRITING` | Hash `gen_k.sav` again; on success delete `.bak` | Mismatch: promote `.bak` back, `FAILED` |

| `WRITTEN` | `WRITTEN` | Main thread observes completion at a tick boundary; `last_save_T` updated | n/a |

**T-6. Every write step is an injection point for the deterministic fault-injection test harness. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* A `.tmp` is matched by the `write_epoch` pattern `gen_<write_epoch>_<k>.tmp` (SL-10); an orphan `.tmp` from an earlier epoch is deleted unless it passes the roll-forward test of the second row. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14)* The scan also reads `slot_epoch.bin` (SL-23 (0)). A leftover `slot

| Crash point | On disk | Recovery |
|---|---|---|
| During `WRITING_TMP` | the position's file (previous generation) intact; a partial `gen_k.tmp` | Delete the `.tmp`; the ring is unchanged |
| After `VERIFYING`, before `SWAPPING_OUT` | the position's file intact; a complete `.tmp` | If the `.tmp` passes its trailer and its `generation` exceeds every generation in the ring, roll forward (run the swap); otherwise delete it |
| Between `SWAPPING_OUT` and `SWAPPING_IN` | `gen_k.bak` (the replaced oldest), a complete `.tmp`, no `gen_k.sav` | `.tmp` valid → promote it into the position and delete the `.bak`; invalid → promote the `.bak` back |
| Between `SWAPPING_IN` and `POST_VERIFY` done | `gen_k.sav` (new) and `gen_k.bak` (replaced oldest) | `gen_k.sav` verifies → delete the `.bak`; else promote the `.bak` |
| During `MANIFEST` | all generations fine; manifest stale or partial | Rebuild the manifest by scanning headers |
| During the `slot_epoch` write *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14)* | `slot_epoch.bin` (old value) intact and a `slot_epoch.tmp` | Delete the `.tmp`; the old value stands |

Candidates after recovery are every `*.sav` plus `*.bak` leftovers, deduplicated by header `generation` (preferring `.sav`); a `.tmp` is never a candidate except through the roll-forward row. The design assumes only that renaming a closed file to an *absent* name is all-or-nothing [UNV]; the ring (at least two verified generations during any swap, since `AUTOSAVE_GENERATIONS` ≥ 2) is the answer to a failed rename.

I need to resolve a tension between the GDD's SL-2 spec, which allows either var_to_bytes or canonical TLV byte form for payloads, and ADR-0005, which is still finalizing the canonical encoding itself. Given TR-shipbody-008 clarifies that canonical bytes are specifically for hashing rather than storage, I'm settling on the container payload form as its own decision.

Looking closer, there's an actual conflict: TR-lsg-022 states saves must never use var_to_bytes, while TR-saveload-003 explicitly allows var_to_bytes(dict) for block payloads. I think the resolution is that each block declares its own payload_form (either VAR or CANON using ADR-0005's TLV), though the GDD's header record schema currently has a closed field list with no room for this, so I'd need to add payload_form as an additional field.

Actually, a cleaner approach avoids touching ADR-0003's descriptor fields entirely: let the form be inferred from whatever type the owner's snapshot returns -- Dictionary gets var_to_bytes, PackedByteArray gets stored raw -- and just record that choice (VAR or RAW, as a 0/1 int) in the per-block header. This way decoding never needs to consult the registry at all.

But at restore time there's a snag: ADR-0003's restore signature expects a Dictionary, so a RAW block's PackedByteArray can't be handed back directly without wrapping it somehow, which feels like an invented shape rather than something ADR-0003 actually specifies. I'm flagging this as an open cross-ADR question -- "RAW block hand-off shape" -- along with a wording conflict I noticed between TR-lsg-022 ("never var_to_bytes") and TR-saveload-003/SL-2. Separately, I'm confirming that var_to_bytes preserves 64-bit integers exactly, so the two-halves rule for values above 2^53 only needs to apply to JSON headers and dev dumps, not to the GDD specs across assembly, section, and shipbody docs that require 64-bit values.

So the resolution is: the 2^53 rule becomes an owner-level lint via ADR rather than a universal walk-time check, since the walk only verifies types not magnitudes, and the dump renders by actual value size. Since var_to_bytes never routes payloads through JSON, the float-cast leniency for integer-valued floats only applies to header/dev-import paths — in the payload path, a float where an int is expected is simply a shape failure.

For header integers I'll require JSON-parsed values to be integral and under 2^53, with 64-bit values carried as hex strings decoded via hex_decode and decode_s64, since hex_to_int fails above 2^63.

For the container layout I'm settling on: an 8-byte magic, a u32 header length, the JSON header, the payload region, and a 32-byte SHA-256 trailer. I'm weighing whether to hash incrementally with HashingContext in chunks or load the whole file (capped around 64MiB, typically ~300KB) into a PackedByteArray and hash the slice excluding the trailer.

For efficiency I'll favor chunked HashingContext.update reads of 64KiB from the file reader rather than slicing a loaded buffer, checking the file length against the 64MiB max save size first via FileAccess.get_length before reading. For the magic bytes I'm deciding on a PNG-style approach: a 6-byte ASCII prefix "SYNSEA" followed by a 0x1A EOF-like byte, avoiding newline characters that could trigger text-mode corruption. I'm keeping the ring buffer at 3 generation slots as per the GDD, and noting that renaming over an existing file works on Windows when unheld but we won't rely on that since a held target just returns a generic ERR_FAILED with no way to distinguish the cause.

For worker threads, I'm spawning one Thread per job and polling is_alive rather than ever joining a live thread, since wait_to_finish only returns immediately if the thread isn't alive -- this avoids hangs on process exit even with a busy thread (probed at 0.68s with a sleeping thread, though in-flight I/O hangs remain unverified). Rather than implementing a true bounded join, I'm treating the "bounded join" requirement as polling with a SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS monotonic deadline before proceeding to shutdown regardless, since Godot's Thread.wait_to_finish has no timeout parameter. I'm holding any abandoned in-flight jobs in a list and deliberately not calling wait on them at exit to accept the "Thread object destroyed without completion realized" warning, and using a Mutex-guarded status record for intermediate state while results are retrieved only through polling is_alive plus wait_to_finish.

Now I'm weighing the snapshot hitch question (OQ-14): the kernel's 16.7ms SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS exceeds the 14.9ms desktop frame budget, and probes show deep-duplicating 32 blocks (~860KB) takes about 2ms plus 1.9ms for var_to_bytes encoding in the editor binary -- though that's not a release export measurement, just indicative. I'm considering three options: splitting capture across frames (forbidden since kernel SAVING must be atomic), accepting a single over-budget frame bounded by SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS and documenting it, or a hybrid where capture stays a synchronous boundary but the post-capture encoding moves to a worker thread, which raises the question of whether handing off a deep-copied Dictionary/Array payload to another thread is actually safe given Godot's atomic refcounting.

I decide moving var_to_bytes to a worker would roughly halve main-thread cost but conflicts with TR-saveload-007's requirement of immutable PackedByteArrays and the 4ms SAVE_ENCODE_BUDGET_MS, so I'll keep encoding on the main thread, log-only bounded by that budget. For OQ-14 I'm landing on option (B): accept the documented bounded over-budget frame, noting it happens at P6 of a RUNNING tick where it's less perceptible, and mitigate further by leaning on the autosave gate that already defers during dialogue plus exploring an incremental capture scheme where blocks with unchanged dirty epochs reuse their previously encoded PackedByteArray instead of re-copying and re-encoding.

This caching idea—keyed on the cached block hash from ADR-0005, letting the kernel skip calling snapshot() entirely for unchanged blocks—is appealing but risks scope creep and correctness bugs if a block mutates without its dirty flag being set, especially since ADR-0004 already enforces a debug invariant that every changed block gets marked dirty. So I'm treating this as a deferred mitigation rather than a settled decision: accept the one over-budget frame for now, gate it behind spike measurements on RM-DECK, and if P99 exceeds threshold, escalate through an ordered list of fixes—skip snapshot() for hash-unchanged blocks, then relax TR-saveload-007 to let the worker own a private deep copy via var_to_bytes, then finally consider a GDD amendment to split capture itself.

I'm flagging this as needing kernel-owner sign-off before proceeding. For the hitch budget, I'm treating the 4ms placeholder versus the 16.7ms-minus-baseline-P99 formula as a soft target rather than a hard cap—the real ceiling is SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS at 16.7ms, with occasional frames over 14.9ms tolerated once per autosave, and this aligns with the GDD's stance that hitches should be non-signalling to the player.

Now I'm working through the restore_epoch mechanics—the slot_epoch.bin format (u32 LE plus a scripted CRC32 using standard polynomial 0xEDB88320, since there's no native CRC32 in ClassDB), the rebuild/advance/carry rules, and the durable-before-request ordering. I'm cross-checking TR-cmd-018, which states restore_epoch is excluded from both the snapshot header and all hashes, against my assumption that a header copy exists for recovery purposes—need to resolve that apparent conflict.

I'm distinguishing between the kernel's snapshot header (the actual state payload) and the file container's header, which carries a read-only write-time copy of restore_epoch per GDD SL-1—the trailer SHA only covers file integrity, not the kernel's state_hash, so this copy never touches the kernel snapshot or any H64 value. I'm flagging this distinction as a clarification needed for TR-cmd-018's wording, and moving on to the kernel-clock block covering world_seed.

For the restore epoch hand-off, I'm defining request_restore with payload, restore_epoch, and expected_state_hash per ADR-0002, including a RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE fault (code 6) for values outside the u32 range—noting that GDScript's 64-bit ints mean u32 values decode as non-negative, which I've confirmed works correctly.

I'm also sketching out the PROFILE file split—same container format but with file_kind PROFILE, no state_hash, a permanent .bak, and zero PROFILE blocks at MVP, tested against a synthetic block with atomic writes.

Now I'm working through the atomic write swap procedure (tmp file, rename existing to permanent .bak, then rename tmp into place) and the migration strategy: container format_version migration via Save/Load with identity mapping at version 1, block schema chains tracked by owning descriptors, and pre-check validation using each descriptor's supported_versions field from ADR-0003 to confirm chain completeness. I'm also deciding how to compute the registry_epoch digest—opting to use SHA-256 truncated to 8 bytes over sorted, newline-separated block_id/schema_version/added_in_format triples via HashingContext directly, rather than coupling it to ADR-0005's TLV format, written out as 16 hex characters. This confirms hash_algo 2 as H64, owned by ADR-0005, representing the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 in little-endian order.

I'm reasoning through how catalogue_version and catalogue_hash should behave: catalogue_hash is diagnostic-only and never gates loading per ADR-0007, while catalogue_version lives in the header but shouldn't gate pre-check directly—restore failures should surface through the owner's own unknown-definition failure path instead. But I realize a save from a newer-catalogue build opened by an older build would otherwise cause spurious quarantine, so I'm deciding that catalogue_version greater than the build's own should trigger a distinct INCOMPATIBLE classification (no quarantine) via a new SL_PRECHECK_CATALOGUE_NEWER reason, flagging this as a recommended addition beyond the GDD's existing pre-check list and an open question for the Save/Load owner.

I'm also working out quarantine counting rules (owner-reported restore failures count toward quarantine after two, but registry_epoch INCOMPATIBLE never quarantines) and the kernel interaction model—pre-check stays pure, staging and restore requests flow through to a K-4 verdict handler, and Save/Load's SL_* refusal reasons form a closed enum in fault domain 1 distinct from kernel faults, which I'm justifying against ADR-0003's registration rules even though Save/Load owns no blocks or hooks.

Now I'm digging into the knob invariant boot checks (I1–I13), weighing whether SL_BOOT_KNOB_RANGE/INVARIANT failures belong to Save/Load's own domain 1 or should be reclassified as domain 2 content-boot errors since the knobs load through ContentLoader as a tuning table—this seems to conflict with ADR-0007's rule against foreign boot codes, so I want to check ADR-0007 §2 for how it handles cross-field tuning invariants before deciding.
