### 3. Contexts: reused, re-armed per call, non-re-entrant

Every kernel-invoked callable receives a context as its last argument and reports only through it. The kernel allocates **one context object per kind at boot and re-arms it before every call**; nothing is allocated per call.

```gdscript
class_name CallContext extends RefCounted          # base; subclasses add methods and override none
var completed: bool
var epoch: int
var faulted: bool:                                  # true if fault() was called here OR on the linked WriteScope
	get: return _faulted or (_scope != null and _scope.faulted)
func put(payload: Variant) -> void                  # snapshot / default_state / read_view / empty_view / binding_source
func fault(code: int, detail: Dictionary = EMPTY_DETAIL) -> void   # packed FAULT_CODE (§ 6); EMPTY_DETAIL is shared and never mutated
func complete() -> CompletionToken                  # sets completed, stamps the armed token's epoch, returns it

class_name ValidateContext extends CallContext      # validate: read-only
func ok() -> void                                   # first outcome stands; a second is CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME
func reject(reason: StringName) -> void             # -> Rejected(VALIDATION_FAILED(reason))

class_name TickContext extends CallContext          # shared base of the two contexts that may submit
var tick: int
func submit_system(type: StringName, payload: Dictionary, dedupe_key: Variant = null) -> void
func has_pending(type: StringName, dedupe_key: Variant = null) -> bool
class_name ApplyContext extends TickContext         # apply
class_name HookContext extends TickContext          # step hooks; adds hook_id
class_name SnapshotContext extends CallContext      # snapshot, restore, post_restore, default_state, init_world,
                                                    # commit_baseline, snap_baseline, binding_source, read_view, empty_view
class_name NotifyContext extends CallContext        # subscriber, result and control-outcome handlers (a fault is counted, never fatal)
```

`submit_system` exists only on `TickContext`, so `validate` cannot submit (it receives a `ValidateContext`) and no "refused call" path is needed.

**Re-arm list.** Before each call the kernel, in one step: increments `epoch`; sets `completed = false`, `_faulted = false`, the outcome (`ok`/`reject`) to none, the `put` payload to none and the fault detail to `EMPTY_DETAIL`; links the context to the call's scope (or to none); and sets a re-entrancy flag. After the call the kernel accepts the result only if the returned value **is** that token (identity), `token.epoch == ctx.epoch` and `ctx.completed` is true. ### F-9. `ring_position`

The `ring_position` formula is defined as:

`gen_next = 1 + max(generation over the ring, the generation number in every `quarantine/` file name, the .demoted files and campaign.json); pos = min{p IN 0 … AUTOSAVE_GENERATIONS − 1 : slot p holds no `.sav` file at all (missing, or its file was moved to `quarantine/`) or holds only a `.demoted` file, AND p is not claimed by an abandoned job} if that set is non-empty, else argmin over the unclaimed p of generation(slot p), excluding the newest generation's slot; if no such p remains, SL_WRITE_NO_POSITION (FAILED, backoff)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `generation` | int | 1 … 2^53 − 1 | header (a JSON number, below 2^53) | Strictly increasing per campaign; the ordering truth, never `T`, never the file name, never modification time |
| `AUTOSAVE_GENERATIONS` ★ | int | 2 … 5, default 3 | Tuning Knobs | Ring size `N` |
| slot `p` | file | `gen_p.sav`, `gen_p.demoted` or empty | the campaign directory | A slot is **free** only if it holds no `.sav` (missing, or the file was moved to `quarantine/`) or holds a `.demoted` file *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: **any other `.sav`, readable or not, occupies it**, so an unreadable but possibly newest file (a transient sharing violation, a file not yet classified) is never targeted or overwritten; a slot **claimed** by an abandoned write job (SL-10) is never chosen until that job reports |

**Output Range:** `gen_next` is monotonic over the life of the campaign even after step-backs (which roll `T` back) and even when the newest file is quarantined and `campaign.json` is lost, because every quarantine file name carries its generation number (SL-19) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; `pos` is in `[0, N − 1]` and the newest generation's file is never renamed or touched, so a window with no newest file cannot exist.

**Example:** `N = 3`; `gen_0.sav` = G7, `gen_1.demoted` = G6 (stepped back from), `gen_2.sav` = G5, and `quarantine/` holds G9 (`STALE_EPOCH`). `gen_next = 1 + max(7, 6, 5, 9) = 10`; slot 1 is the first free position, so G10 is written to `gen_1.sav` and the `.demoted` occupant is renamed `.bak` and deleted after `POST_VERIFY` (T-4).

# ADR-0006: Save Container, Generations, Versioning and Restore Epoch

## Status
Proposed

## Date
2026-10-28

## Last Verified
2026-10-28 (against `design/gdd/save-load-and-versioned-format.md` SL-1 to SL-25, T-3 to T-6, F-5, F-8, F-9 and the Tuning Knobs tables; `docs/architecture/tr-baseline.md` rows citing ADR-0006; ADR-0001, ADR-0002 § 6, ADR-0003 §§ 3, 6, 9 and ADR-0007 § 3.4; `docs/engine-reference/godot/` `VERSION.md`, `breaking-changes.md`, `deprecated-apis.md`). The pinned engine reference has no core, file-I/O or threading module, so every engine claim here rests either on a probe run on the installed 4.7.2 editor on 2026-10-28 (marked **probed**) or on training knowledge (marked **UNVERIFIED**, with the spike that settles it). No game code exists. All probes were synthetic, headless, on a development machine with an editor binary; none is a release-export measurement.

## Decision Makers
Claude (author), running under `modes.automation: autonomous` (`project.yaml`); decisions logged for the user's review; the user has not yet reviewed this ADR. Engine-specialist and technical-director review: pending (joint review of ADR-0004 to ADR-0010 and this ADR). See Review Log.

## Summary
Sixty-five requirements from seventeen GDDs need a save file that is self-verifying, written without ever endangering a good generation, versioned from the first build, and paired with a per-slot `restore_epoch` that re-keys threat draws on death without letting quit or death be a reroll oracle. This ADR fixes one container (8-byte magic, JSON header, `var_to_bytes` block payloads, SHA-256 trailer), a ring of three generations written by one `Thread` per job that the main thread only polls, a two-level version scheme (container migrated by Save/Load, blocks by their owners), a PROFILE side file in the same container, and `slot_epoch.bin` made durable before every `request_restore`.

## Context

### Problem Statement
The game's one failure consequence is death and restart from the last autosave (Pillar 5), and its horror depends on the player never being able to read the world through the save system (Pillars 1, 3, 4). That makes persistence unusually load-bearing: a bad write that costs a good generation destroys the campaign; a pause when the game saves tells the player a tell has closed; a restart that replays the identical threat draws makes death a free retry; a restart that lets quit choose the draws makes quit a reroll oracle; and a format that cannot be migrated strands every outside tester at the first schema change. The Save/Load GDD settles the behaviour and defers a dozen mechanism choices to "the atomic write, backup and thread model" ADR and to "the container ADR": what the bytes are, how a Windows rename is used safely, how a worker thread is owned, how a quit is waited for, how the 64-bit and JSON constraints are met, where `restore_epoch` lives and how it reaches the kernel, and whether the snapshot hitch is acceptable. Two probes (§ Engine Compatibility) also falsify two GDD sentences: `var_to_bytes` does encode objects, and `FileAccess.open` is not exclusive. Without one decision, each of the 14 persisted blocks would meet a slightly different container, and the first outside build would find the differences.

### Constraints
- **Save/Load registers zero state blocks and zero hooks** (SL-17, TR-saveload-018): ring bookkeeping must live outside the world, or it rolls back with a restore.
- **Exactly one thread boundary** exists (architecture § Data Flow 7): the save writer. `Thread`, `WorkerThreadPool` and `call_deferred` into kernel code are lint-forbidden elsewhere (CR-1a). The worker receives immutable `PackedByteArray`s, paths and integers only (TR-saveload-007).
- **Capture is synchronous inside the kernel's `SAVING` state** at a tick boundary (TR-cmd-017, TR-saveload-009); `SAVING` is atomic within one boundary service and never spans a frame (ADR-0003 § 9, ADR-0001 § 1).
- **A bad file never produces `FAULTED`** (TR-saveload-014): the pre-check is a pure function of `(bytes, registry view, build constants)` and runs before the kernel is touched.
- **Block objects are `RefCounted`, restore copies into the existing object** (registry `block_as_resource_or_node`; ADR-0003 § 2). No `Resource` or `.tres` path, ever (a script can ride in one).
- **Integer-only simulation** (ADR-0005 forward); JSON parses numbers as `float` (probed), so no 64-bit or hashed value may travel as a JSON number (S-1).
- **No wall clock in any sim decision** (kernel H9); millisecond I/O timeouts read an injected monotonic source and change no sim state (SL-23).
- **No autoload or static singleton** (registry `kernel_autoload_or_global`): Save/Load is constructed and injected by the composition root.
- **Fault codes** follow ADR-0003 § 6: `(DOMAIN_ID << 16) | local`, domain 1 = `save_load`, append-only.
- **Single player at MVP**; co-op replication, guest carry-over and Steam Auto-Cloud are later tiers and constrain only the path layout.

### Requirements
- One container format for WORLD generations and the PROFILE store, self-verifying by a trailer that lives outside the header.
- A write that never overwrites in place, never deletes a generation before its successor verified, never blocks the main thread, and never starts while the kernel is `FAULTED`.
- A load that classifies every failure (corrupt, incompatible, owner-failed, not-reproduced) and decides the next action from the class.
- Two-level versioning with an obligation to migrate that begins at the first outside build, and development saves that are refused rather than half-migrated.
- `restore_epoch` that survives a process kill, a lost manifest and a step-back, is durable before the restore that uses it, and reaches the sim only as an argument.
- A quit that waits for its write by polling, with a timeout, and never hangs the process on a stuck worker.
- A recorded ruling on the snapshot hitch (OQ-14) and a named spike for every engine claim the reference does not source.

## Decision

The decision has three parts, numbered so each can be reviewed on its own: **§ 1 the container and the write path**, **§ 2 versioning and migration**, **§ 3 the restore epoch**. Behaviour already fixed by the GDD (SL-1 to SL-25, T-3 to T-9, F-1 to F-10) is cited, not restated; this ADR decides what the GDD left as `[UNV]`, as an "ADR candidate", or wrong.

### Architecture Diagram

```
 main thread                                           worker thread (one Thread per WriteJob)
 ───────────                                           ───────────────────────────────────────
 composition root (ADR-0001)
   │ constructs SaveService (RefCounted, no scene tree)
   │ and SaveHost (Node, PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS, priority 0)
   ▼
 SaveHost._process  ── polls (frame, after TickDriver)
   │  gates (SL-5) / triggers (SL-4)
   ▼
 ControlHandle.request_snapshot ──► kernel boundary service: RUNNING/PAUSED → SAVING → PRIOR
   │                                   every persist block: snapshot(ctx) → ctx.put(Dictionary)   (deep copies)
   │◄── ControlOutcome{payload} ───────┘   [kernel cost: capture_time, inside SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS]
   │ split by persist_scope: WORLD → generation image, PROFILE → profile image
   │ per block: var_to_bytes(dict) → PackedByteArray        [main thread: t_file_encode ≤ 4 ms, log-only]
   │ hand-off: bytes + paths + ints ───────────────────────► WriteJob.run()
   │                                                           per-block SHA-256, header JSON, trailer
   │ poll status (Mutex-guarded record, is_alive())            write gen_<we>_<k>.tmp → flush → close
   │◄───────────── WRITTEN / FAILED ───────────────────────    re-read, re-hash, decode + type walk
   │                                                           position's file → .bak (if any)
   │                                                           .tmp → gen_k.sav (target absent)
   │                                                           re-hash gen_k.sav, delete .bak, campaign.json
   ▼
 save_status  (host-local read)

 Load / death stub:  candidates → PreCheck.run(bytes, registry_view, build)  (pure, before the kernel)
   → stage decoded blocks (hot copy, SL-11) → epoch staging (§ 3.3: slot_epoch.bin on the worker, polled)

   → kernel LOADING (owners restore + post_restore) → K-4 verdict in ControlOutcome → RUNNING
```

### 1. The container and the write path

**1.1 Layout.** The file layout is SL-1 as written: 8 bytes of magic, `u32` LE `header_len`, UTF-8 JSON header, concatenated block payloads, a 32-byte SHA-256 trailer over every preceding byte (the **format law**: for every layout, forever, the last 32 bytes of any file bearing the magic prefix hash `[0, size - 32)`). Choices this ADR adds:

- **Magic.** `53 59 4E 53 45 41 1A` (`"SYNSEA"` and a SUB/EOF byte, so a text-mode tool stops early), then the container-layout id byte (`01` for `FORMAT_VERSION` 1). The file extension is `.sav`.
- **Hashing is streamed.** The trailer, `payload_sha256` and `state_hash` inputs use `HashingContext` (`HASH_SHA256`) fed in chunks (`update`) so no hash needs a second whole-file copy; reading a candidate checks `FileAccess.get_length()` against `MAX_SAVE_BYTES` first, then reads. Whole-file reads use `get_buffer` loops or `FileAccess.get_file_as_bytes`; both are acceptable, the length cap comes first.
- **One payload form.** Every block payload is `var_to_bytes(dictionary)` of the owner's plain-data snapshot. The GDD's second form ("the owner's own canonical byte form as raw bytes", SL-2) is **dropped as a separate container form**: a block that publishes canonical bytes (the Graph's `canonical_bytes()`) puts them in its snapshot dictionary as a `PackedByteArray` field, which `var_to_bytes` stores byte-exact. Reason: one decode path, one type walk, and a restore hand-off that is always a `Dictionary`, matching ADR-0003's `restore(data: Dictionary, stored_version, ctx)` (no `form` field and no byte-blob hand-off shape to invent). Cost: an 8-byte wrapper per such block. The canonical bytes are **hash input only** (ADR-0005); the stored bytes are never canonical, and State equality is `state_hash`, never file bytes (probed: insertion order changes the bytes).
- **Header** is the closed list of SL-1 plus the additions of § 2 (`catalogue_version` is already there). Unknown extra keys are ignored when `min_reader_version` is satisfied; a missing required key refuses.

**1.2 Interchange and the trust model (corrects SL-2).**

1. **The encoder does not refuse objects (probed).** `var_to_bytes` silently encodes an `Object` as an `EncodedObjectAsID` and `bytes_to_var` returns it. SL-2's wording "the form that does not encode objects" is wrong in the direction that matters: a stray object in a `snapshot()` would reach disk. The defence is therefore **not** the encoder. It is (a) the type walk, which rejects `TYPE_OBJECT` explicitly (an `EncodedObjectAsID` is an Object), and (b) the write-side `VERIFYING` stage, which decodes and walks the bytes the worker just wrote (T-4), so an object-bearing snapshot is caught at write (`SL_WRITE_UNENCODABLE`, previous generations intact) and never first at a death.
2. **Decode with `bytes_to_var` only.** `var_to_bytes_with_objects` and `bytes_to_var_with_objects` are forbidden outright, as are `Resource`, `.tres`, `.res` and `ResourceLoader` for any save path. `bytes_to_var` of hostile input returns `null` and logs an engine `ERROR` that code cannot suppress (probed): so the decode runs only **after** the trailer, the block table and `payload_sha256` have passed, and a `null` result for a block that must be a `Dictionary` is `SL_PRECHECK_BLOCK_DECODE_FAILED`. A forged file with correct hashes can still produce engine error lines; that is a tamper case, accepted, and the fuzz suite is told (Risks, ADR-0010 assumption).
3. **Allowed types, enforced by the walk, not the encoder (probed: `Vector2i` round-trips, so the ban is policy).** `null`, `bool`, `int` (full 64 bits, § 1.3), finite `float`, `String`, `Array`, `Dictionary` with `String` or `int` keys, and the packed arrays `PackedByteArray`, `PackedInt32Array`, `PackedInt64Array`. Forbidden: `Vector2i` and every vector or rect, `Color`, `Object`, `Callable`, `Signal`, `RID`, `NodePath`, `StringName` (a `StringName` is decoded as one, probed, so it must be rejected, not coerced), and non-finite floats. Typed `Array[T]` and `Dictionary[K, V]` **survive** the encoder (probed), which settles SL-2's "untyped until the spike" note: snapshots may use typed or untyped containers; the walk checks the decoded element types either way. Bounds: `MAX_DECODE_DEPTH` 16, `MAX_DECODE_NODES` 250 000 (a packed array counts as one node), per `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES` and `MAX_SAVE_BYTES`. Owners' `restore()` still validates meaning; the walk validates only type and size.
4. **JSON appears only in the header and in the dev-only `dump-save`.** A dump renders any `int` whose magnitude is at or above 2^53 as a lowercase decimal string and any `PackedByteArray` as `Marshalls.raw_to_base64`; it is diagnostics, never a load path (TR-lsg-022).
5. **No compression** in the MVP (`codec` 0; 1 reserved). A size alarm at `SAVE_SIZE_ALARM_BYTES` 2 MiB is diagnostics only.

**1.3 64-bit values.** Two rules, one per medium.

- **Header (JSON).** Every value that can reach 2^53 (`T`, `world_seed`, `state_hash`, per-block hashes, `campaign_id`, `registry_epoch`) is an exact-width lowercase hex string (16 chars for 64 bits, 32 for 128). **Decoding is `String.hex_decode()` followed by a size check (8 or 16 bytes) and `PackedByteArray.decode_s64` or `decode_u64`; never `String.hex_to_int`** (probed: it saturates to `INT64_MAX` with an error on 16 `f`s). A `world_seed` or hash with the top bit set therefore reads as a negative GDScript `int`; that is correct, not a bug, and every consumer compares as `int`. Header numbers that stay numbers (`format_version`, `schema_version`, `generation`, lengths, offsets, counts, `hash_algo`, `codec`, `tick_rate`, `restore_epoch`) arrive as `float` from the parser and must be integral and **strictly below 2^53** before conversion; a value of 2^53 or more is refused (probed: `9007199254740993` parses to `9007199254740992.0`, so the first ambiguous value is exactly 2^53, which the strict bound catches).
- **Payload (binary).** `var_to_bytes` carries `int` at full 64-bit width exactly (probed with 2^53+1 and `PackedInt64Array`). The binary container therefore **accepts native `int64` in block payloads**; the "two 32-bit halves or strings" convention of TR-section-006, TR-assembly-013 and TR-shipbody-007 came from the JSON constraint and is **legal but not required**. S-1 is restated as: no float ever stands in for an integer, and a field that may reach 2^53 must be declared `int64` in its owner's snapshot schema so that `dump-save` (and any future JSON export) renders it as a string. This relaxes TR-saveload-017 and TR-sanity-020's "values stay below 2^53" for payload fields; it keeps it for everything JSON can touch. A float where an `int` is expected is a restore `SHAPE`-class failure of the owner (the sim is integer-only); an owner may still accept an integral float when importing from a dev JSON fixture, not from a binary payload.

**1.4 The ring and the campaign directory.** `user://saves/<campaign_id>/` holds `campaign.json` (a rebuildable hint, never truth, SL-3), `gen_0.sav` to `gen_{N-1}.sav` with `N` = `AUTOSAVE_GENERATIONS` 3, transient `gen_<write_epoch>_<k>.tmp` and `gen_<k>.bak`, `gen_<k>.demoted`, `slot_epoch.bin` and `slot_epoch.tmp`, `profile.sav` with a permanent `profile.bak`, `campaign.lock`, and `quarantine/`. **Order is the header `generation` number, never file name, mtime or `T`** (TR-saveload-005). Positions are chosen by F-9. Two encodings the GDD left open (OQ-27) are decided here:

- **Quarantine reason is in the file name:** `quarantine/g<generation>_<REASON>_<k>.sav`, `REASON` in {`CORRUPT`, `RESTORE_FAILED`, `STALE_EPOCH`}. `gen_next` reads the generation from the name without opening the file (SL-19). No sidecar and no manifest entry: a manifest is a hint and a sidecar can be lost separately from the file.
- **Retiring a campaign** renames its directory to `user://saves_retired/<campaign_id>/`, out of the active location, never deleting; `delete_campaign` is the separate hold-to-confirm action. The retired directory keeps the same layout so a retired campaign is restorable by hand.

**1.5 The write protocol, with what the probes change.** The sequence is T-4 as written (`CAPTURING`, `WRITING_TMP`, `VERIFYING`, `SWAPPING_OUT`, `SWAPPING_IN`, `POST_VERIFY`, `MANIFEST`, `WRITTEN`/`FAILED`), run on the worker. What the probes settle:

- **Rename over an existing, unlocked target works on Windows (probed)** and replaces atomically from the caller's point of view. The generation swap still **never relies on it**: it renames the position's old file to `.bak`, then renames `.tmp` to a now-absent name. The reason is not rename correctness but **the failure cases**: a target held open by an antivirus or indexer fails with `ERR_FAILED` and leaves the target intact (probed with a READ-held proxy), and the `.bak` step makes every partial state recoverable by T-6 (at least two verified generations exist during any swap, since `N` >= 2). Whether a crash-time replace is atomic on NTFS is **UNVERIFIED** (SAVE-WRK-1 b).
- **`slot_epoch.bin` and `campaign.json` use rename-over** (temp, flush, close, rename over the live name, re-read): a failure of that rename is `ERR_FAILED` with the old file intact (probed), which is the intended outcome. Both are recoverable by rule (§ 3.4 and SL-3), so the cheaper protocol is safe for them and only for them.
- **All `ERR_FAILED` are alike.** `DirAccess` reports a sharing violation, a missing parent and a permission error with the same code (probed: 1). Retries are therefore `RENAME_RETRY_COUNT` 3, `RENAME_RETRY_DELAY_MS` 50 on the worker for any rename failure, and the failure class is "rename failed", not a guessed cause.
- **Every `store_*` and `flush` result is checked** (`store_*` return `bool` since 4.4, sourced). `flush()` followed by `close()` then a re-open and re-hash is the "verified" definition; it proves readability through the operating system's cache, **not durability** (**UNVERIFIED**: whether `flush` implies an fsync; SAVE-WRK-1 c). The ring and T-6 recovery are the answer to power loss.
- **Temp names carry `write_epoch`** (`gen_<write_epoch>_<k>.tmp`, SL-10): an abandoned job's temp file and a later job's can never be the same file.

**1.6 The worker: one `Thread` per job, polled, never joined while alive.**

- **Model.** One `Thread` per `WriteJob`, its handle held on a `RefCounted` `WriteJob` that also carries the status record. `Thread.start(callable.bind(blocks, paths, ints))` with `PackedByteArray` arguments (probed: works, the caller's array is unchanged; packed arrays are copy-on-write, so the main thread must drop its reference and never mutate after hand-off). **`WorkerThreadPool` is rejected**: it offers no timed wait and its tasks cannot be abandoned individually (training knowledge; **UNVERIFIED** against 4.7, ADR-0010 may confirm). The Save/Load module is the **one** place `Thread` is legal; ADR-0010's lint carries that single exception, scoped to the module's directory.
- **Status record.** `{state, write_epoch, generation, position, result_code, finish_or_abort}` guarded by one `Mutex`; the worker writes `state` at each T-4 stage, the main thread reads it and writes only `finish_or_abort` (SL-10, `DOWNED` entry). The worker never calls `call_deferred`, never touches a `Node`, never calls back (probed: no callback needed).
- **Polling.** A tick-boundary poll in `RUNNING` and a frame poll from `SaveHost` in `PAUSED`, `SAVING`, `LOADING` and the quit wait. `SaveHost` is a `Node` with `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` at the engine-default priority 0 (after `TICK_DRIVER`), so every observation follows the driver's boundary service in the same frame. That the frame poll fires in `PAUSED` and `LOADING` is **UNVERIFIED** (needs a scene tree; SAVE-WRK-1 e).
- **Reaping.** Each poll calls `wait_to_finish()` **only** on a job whose thread reports `not is_alive()` (probed: returns at once with the callable's value). A dead thread with no terminal `WRITTEN`/`FAILED` status is `SL_WRITE_WORKER_DIED`: `save_status` `FAILED`, `fail_n` + 1, the ring position released, the `.tmp` left to T-6. **A live thread is never joined**: `Thread.wait_to_finish` and the pool wait take no timeout (training knowledge), so a join at the `DEAD` boundary could hang the frame on a hung write.
- **Abandonment** is SL-10 as written (`write_epoch` bump, position claimed, `MAX_LIVE_ABANDONED_JOBS` 2, `WRITE_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS` 30 000, `DEATH_STUB_WRITE_WAIT_MS` 5 000). A job that lands a generation after being abandoned is moved to `quarantine/` as `STALE_EPOCH`.
- **Quit during a write: "bounded join" is bounded polling.** Process exit does not wait on a busy worker (probed: an 8 s sleeping worker did not delay exit past 0.68 s; the engine prints a `~Thread` WARNING and an ObjectDB leak report, which are expected and are ADR-0010's to allow-list). Save & Quit therefore **polls** the `QUIT` job under `SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS` 3 000 on the monotonic source and calls `request_shutdown` on `WRITTEN`; on timeout it does not abandon (a late completion is simply a `QUIT` generation, SL-6), reports `FAILED`, and the Chart Table offers the hold-to-confirm "quit without saving". An abandoned worker still running at exit is left to the operating system and its `.tmp` handled by T-6 on the next open. A worker blocked in a syscall rather than a sleep is **UNVERIFIED** (SAVE-WRK-1 d).

**1.7 Single-instance lock (corrects SL-10).** The GDD's `campaign.lock` "created with an exclusive open" is **not implementable with `FileAccess`**: a second WRITE-open of the same path succeeds (and truncates; probed). What does work on Windows (probed): a file held open makes `rename_absolute` and `remove_absolute` of it fail with `ERR_FAILED`, for READ and WRITE handles alike. The lock is therefore: the process that opens a campaign keeps a `FileAccess` handle on `campaign.lock` open (write mode, containing its process id, diagnostic only) for the campaign's lifetime; a second process tests ownership by renaming the file to `campaign.lock.probe` and back; a failure means "held", and it opens the campaign **READ_ONLY** (SL-10, AC-SL-147). A crashed holder releases its handle with the process, so there is no stale-lock case and no process-id liveness check is needed (`OS.is_process_running` is probed true for the own id, but whether it answers for a foreign non-child process is **UNVERIFIED** and is not used). On Linux and the Deck, rename of an open file is expected to succeed (**UNVERIFIED**, SAVE-WRK-1 g), so the lock gives no protection there; Steam launches a single instance by default, and the second-process exposure is recorded, not engineered around.

**1.8 The PROFILE split.** SL-9 as written: one kernel snapshot, split by `persist_scope` at write time; WORLD blocks to the generation, PROFILE blocks to `profile.sav` (same container, `file_kind` `PROFILE`, no `state_hash`, no `restore_epoch`), same atomic procedure with a **ring of one plus a permanent `.bak`** (the swap keeps the `.bak` instead of deleting it). An in-session restore passes **only WORLD blocks** to `request_restore`, so PROFILE blocks are never rolled back (TR-cmd-017, TR-saveload-019); a cold open loads each scope whole from its own file. A profile write is triggered when a capture's PROFILE per-block hashes differ from those last written (ADR-0005's cached block hashes; no subscription), on `QUIT`, and at most every `PROFILE_MIN_WRITE_GAP_TICKS` 300. **Zero PROFILE blocks ship at MVP**; the mechanism is built and tested with a synthetic PROFILE block. `scope` (SHARED/PER_PLAYER) and `persist_scope` (WORLD/PROFILE) are orthogonal: `suit.state`, `sanity.state` and `sanity.ledger` are PER_PLAYER x WORLD and roll back with the death stub (TR-suit-029, TR-webmap-030).

**1.9 Capture cost and the snapshot hitch (OQ-14).** The kernel owns capture (`SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS` 16.7, a ceiling, kernel GDD). Save/Load adds on the main thread only `var_to_bytes` per block (`t_file_encode`, log threshold `SAVE_ENCODE_BUDGET_MS` 4) and the hand-off (`t_handoff`, at most `WRITE_HANDOFF_MAX_FRACTION` 0.05 of the budget); SHA-256 of payloads, the header and the trailer are worker work (T-4, F-5). **Ruling (proposed, for the kernel owner to confirm): keep `SAVING` atomic, accept one over-budget frame per autosave, document it, and let SAVE-WRK-1 f measure it.** Evidence, all synthetic and probed: encode of 860 KB of synthetic block data 1.9 ms, deep copy 2.0 ms, SHA-256 of 300 KiB 0.7 ms, decode 3.5 ms; the MVP slice is 14 blocks and about 86 KiB to 300 KiB (SL-19), so the Save/Load-owned share of the hitch is of order 1 to 2 ms against the 4 ms threshold. The unmeasured share is the owners' real `snapshot()` implementations and the capture-time `H64` hash, which is the kernel's. A 32-block snapshot reaching 16.7 ms (TR-cmd-032) therefore exceeds the 14.9 ms desktop frame target for **one frame per autosave** and no more; the autosave gate already keeps that frame away from tells (SL-5). **Mitigation rungs, in order, only if the spike shows the frame is visible (P99 above `16.7 - P99(baseline CPU frame work)`, the formula already in `SAVE_HITCH_BUDGET_MS`):** (1) the kernel skips `snapshot()` for a block whose cached hash (ADR-0005) is unchanged since the last capture and reuses the previous encoded bytes (needs ADR-0004's debug check that every changed block marked a dirty key, and ADR-0005's cached hashes); (2) move `var_to_bytes` to the worker, which relaxes TR-saveload-007 from "only `PackedByteArray`s" to "plus one Save/Load-owned, never-again-touched deep copy" (OQ-53 a: `snapshot()` returns caller-owned data); (3) split capture across frames, which the kernel's atomic-`SAVING` rule forbids today and needs a kernel GDD amendment. Rungs 2 and 3 are not decided here.

**1.10 Pre-check, recovery and failure classes.** T-5 (the 23-step ordered pre-check), T-6 (crash recovery) and the failure classes of SL-11 stand as written. This ADR adds three things:

- **A newer catalogue is INCOMPATIBLE, not owner-failed.** After `min_reader_version` and before the block table: a header `catalogue_version` greater than the running build's is `SL_PRECHECK_CATALOGUE_NEWER`, class INCOMPATIBLE, stop, no quarantine ("made by a newer build"). Without it, a downgrade would surface as `GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF` or `SUIT_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF`, an *owner-reported* failure that quarantines a good file after `QUARANTINE_AFTER_FAILURES` 2. A *lower or equal* version proceeds: owners resolve renamed defs through ADR-0007's alias path. `catalogue_hash` is diagnostic only and never gates a load.
- **The pre-check is a pure static function** `PreCheck.run(bytes: PackedByteArray, registry: RegistryView, build: BuildConstants) -> PreCheckResult`, no clock, no file handle, no `Node`, unit-tested over in-memory byte arrays (TR-saveload-014). `RegistryView` is a plain-data snapshot of `(block_id, supported_versions, persist_scope, persist, added_in_format)` triples that Save/Load builds once after the registry freeze.
- **Reproduction mismatch stays a diagnostic.** The kernel's K-4 verdict arrives in `ControlOutcome` (ADR-0002 § 6); `SL_VERIFY_NOT_REPRODUCED` is never a fallback reason (TR-saveload-015).

**1.11 Fault domain 1 and the closed reason sets.** `src/<save module>/save_load_faults.gd` (`class_name SaveLoadFaults extends RefCounted`, `const DOMAIN_ID := 1`, packed codes, `NAMES`) holds the closed sets `SL_PRECHECK_*`, `SL_WRITE_*`, `SL_LOAD_*`, `SL_VERIFY_*`, `SL_EPOCH_*`, `SL_QUIT_*`, `SL_NEW_GAME_*` and `SL_BOOT_*`, and Save/Load calls `register_fault_domain(1, &"save_load", NAMES)` in `BOOTING` so diagnostics print `save_load.PRECHECK_FILE_SHA_MISMATCH`. **None of these faults the kernel**: a bad file, a failed write and a refused quit are values and diagnostics, and the kernel's own codes (`CAPTURE_ERROR` 7, `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE` 6, `RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BLOCK` 4, `TICK_RATE_MISMATCH` 5, all domain 0) are the unreachable backstops behind Save/Load's pre-check. Registering a domain is neither a block nor a hook, so TR-saveload-018 holds. Knob range and invariant failures (`SL_BOOT_KNOB_RANGE`, `SL_BOOT_KNOB_INVARIANT`) are **domain 2** content boot errors raised by the ADR-0007 `ScalarTable` machinery (TR-saveload-024 is ADR-0007's); only the cross-check of § 2.3, which needs the live registry, raises domain 1 `SL_BOOT_*`.

**1.12 The host API and what Save/Load may observe.** SL-21 as written: `new_game(world_seed)`, `continue_campaign()`, `save_and_quit()`, `cancel_held_close()`, read-only `campaign_info()`, `list_saves()`, `retire_campaign`, `delete_campaign`, and the host-local reads `save_status`, `fail_escalated`, `SaveInfo`, `restore_reason`, `restore_epoch` (diagnostic), `quit_held`, `quit_write_active`. No `save_now`, no `load(generation)` outside dev builds, no command registered (TR-saveload-023). Save/Load is a **control-plane caller, not a subscriber** (SL-13): it holds a `ControlHandle` and a `save_load` facet of read views limited to `kernel.clock`, `controller.state.loco_state`, `graph` failures, `attention.view`, `suit` `vitals_state`, Assembly's `ragged_breach_open()` and `last_shape_change_T()`, Interaction's `last_salvage_T()`, and it never reads a `PERCEPTION_OUT` view or writes a block. It uses `ControlHandle.set_outcome_handler` for the snapshot payload and the K-4 verdict.

### 2. Versioning and migration

**2.1 Two levels, as SL-14.** `format_version` (container) is migrated by Save/Load; `schema_version` (per block) is migrated only by the owner inside `restore(data, stored_version, ctx)` as a chain of registered pure functions `(old Dictionary) -> new Dictionary`. Save/Load never rewrites block data. `min_reader_version` equals `format_version` on every write in the MVP. A migrated payload is **not written back** to the old file; the next autosave writes the new shape, so a downgrade-then-upgrade cannot half-migrate a file.

**2.2 The block contract in ADR-0003 terms.** Reconciling SL-15 with the registered owner-callable contract (ADR-0003 § 1, registry `owner_callable_contract`): a persisted block registers `snapshot`, `restore`, `default_state` and `post_restore` as `Callable`s each returning `ctx.complete()`, with `supported_versions`, `persist_scope` and `restore_after` in its `BlockDescriptor`.

- `snapshot(ctx)` calls `ctx.put(payload: Dictionary)`: a deep copy (no aliasing of live state, so the encode may later leave the main thread), plain data per § 1.2, rows sorted by id, no derived caches, no object references, transient fields normalised (TR-pc-020).
- `restore(data: Dictionary, stored_version: int, ctx)` is **two-phase: decode and validate into scratch, then copy the contents into the existing block object**. This is the single wording of the rule; "whole-block replace" and "swaps whole tables from scratch" in owner GDDs mean *replace the block's contents*, never the object (registry `block_as_resource_or_node`; ADR-0003 § 2: read-view facades are long-lived).
- **Failure is reported through `ctx.fault(<OWNER>_RESTORE_*)`** with the owner's domain code and a named detail, never by return value and never by clamping; the kernel fires `load_failed` and Save/Load maps it to the `RESTORE_FAILED` class of SL-11. Owner GDDs that describe `(ok, reason, detail)` mean this (ADR-0003 sync, not this ADR's to change).
- `post_restore(ctx)` rebuilds derived caches and cross-block verification; `default_state(ctx)` fills a block missing from an older file whose `added_in_format` exceeds the file's `format_version`.
- A restore is idempotent: `snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` is canonical-byte identical except for the closed `REBASE_BLOCKS` list (SL-12), and the Graph's, Body's and Controller's tests prove it.

**2.3 Block versions are data, cross-checked at boot.** `added_in_format`, `RETIRED_BLOCKS` and the mandatory flag live in one committed file `assets/data/saveload/block_versions.json` (loaded by ADR-0007's pipeline as a closed-schema table), not in `BlockDescriptor`, so ADR-0003's descriptor field list is unchanged. After the registry freeze, the composition root runs `SaveBootCheck.verify(block_versions, registry_view)`: a mandatory-derivation mismatch, a registered block that is also retired (`SL_BOOT_RETIRED_BUT_REGISTERED`), or a missing entry fails boot with a domain-1 `SL_BOOT_*` code and the root never starts the kernel. A persisted WORLD block is **mandatory iff its `added_in_format` is at most the file's `format_version`**; the MVP set in SL-25 is the *result* of that rule, not a hand-kept list.

**2.4 `registry_epoch` and `catalogue_version`.** `registry_epoch` (the header field that tells "the registry moved" from corruption) is the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 over the UTF-8 text of the sorted lines `block_id:schema_version:added_in_format\n` for every persisted block, as lowercase hex. It uses `HashingContext` directly, **not** H64 or the canonical encoding, so it depends on neither ADR-0005 nor the kernel. A file whose `registry_epoch` differs from the running build's and fails a mandatory-set or schema step is INCOMPATIBLE-dev: never CORRUPT, never quarantined (SL-11, T-5 steps 18 and 21). `catalogue_version` is the Item DB's single integer offered by ADR-0007 § 3.4; it is written in the header as an `int`, and its only gating use is the newer-than-build refusal of § 1.10.

**2.5 `hash_algo` and `codec`.** `hash_algo` 2 names H64 (the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 via `HashingContext`, read little-endian, ratified by the GDD, owned by ADR-0005); 0 and 1 are reserved, never written. An unsupported `hash_algo` skips the reproduction compare (`SL_VERIFY_ALGO_SKIPPED`, REBASED cause 4) so a kernel hash change is never a save-breaking event. `codec` 0 only.

**2.6 Policy and fixtures (SL-14, unchanged).** The migration machinery exists from format 1. Two goldens: `tests/fixtures/saves/v1-standin/` (regenerated freely until the registry settles) and `tests/fixtures/saves/v1/` (generated from the real registry at the first outside build, immutable, with a CI schema-drift fingerprint: the `registry_epoch` of the committed shapes may change only together with a `schema_version` or `format_version` bump). The obligation to migrate begins with the first build given to anyone outside the project; before it, a mismatched development save is refused as "made by an incompatible development build". This is the same moment ADR-0007's id ledgers flip to `SHIPPED`; one project-level decision flips both.

### 3. The restore epoch

**3.1 Ownership and storage.** Save/Load owns `restore_epoch`, an unsigned 32-bit integer (an `int` in `[0, 2^32 - 1]`) starting at 0 at `new_game` (SL-18). It lives in the per-slot side file `user://saves/<campaign_id>/slot_epoch.bin`: **8 bytes, the value as `u32` LE then its CRC32 as `u32` LE**, written by the worker as `slot_epoch.tmp`, flush, close, rename over `slot_epoch.bin`, re-read with a valid CRC (that re-read is the `EPOCH_DURABLE` report). **CRC32 is hand-rolled** (polynomial `0xEDB88320`, init and final XOR `0xFFFFFFFF`, bitwise, over 4 bytes): `PackedByteArray` has no `crc32` (probed), the scripted loop matched the standard check vector and costs about 1 microsecond, and a truncated 4-byte hash was rejected as a gratuitous change to the GDD's 8-byte format. The vector `crc32("123456789") == 0xCBF43926` is a unit test. The file is in no generation, so no generation's bytes, trailer, `state_hash` or any key derived from them changes after `VERIFYING`; this is what makes SL-12's REBASED baseline key stable (R14). Each WORLD generation's header carries a **read-only write-time copy** (`restore_epoch`, an int below 2^32) used only by the rebuild rule of § 3.4; it is never rewritten.

**3.2 When it advances (R13, unchanged).** A death-stub restore and a `FAULT_RECOVERY` always advance it. A Continue (`LOAD_GAME`) advances it unless the generation it restores is a `QUIT` generation that is the newest non-demoted verified generation: that Continue **carries the epoch unchanged and writes nothing**, so Save & Quit then Continue replays the threat draws an uninterrupted run would meet and quit buys nothing. An advance is `restore_epoch := min(2^32 - 1, max(e_mem, e_slot) + 1)`, saturating and logging at the top; a step-back, a demotion, a quarantine or a lost manifest cannot lower it. A stub that finds nothing loadable restores nothing and does not advance it. The Graph's physical failures and every persisted counter never read the epoch.

**3.3 Durable before the restore is requested (R14, with the polling decided).** After selection, pre-check and staging, Save/Load computes the new value and hands the `slot_epoch.bin` write to the worker **as its own job**, never queued behind a generation write or an abandoned job, and polls it once per frame from `SaveHost` (never blocking, never joined). Only on `EPOCH_DURABLE` does it call `ControlHandle.request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash)`, so the kernel's `LOADING` holds no wait on Save/Load I/O and stays atomic within one boundary service. On the death stub the kernel is `RUNNING` from the `DEAD` boundary to that call (at most `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` 500, 30 frames); the seat stays `DEAD`, the hard gate is closed, and a `restore_pending` latch refuses every capture and pause request and answers a further trigger with `SL_LOAD_REENTRANT`. The Player Controller's DEAD hand-off (TR-pc-022) is honoured only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`.

**3.4 Failure and recovery.**
- **Write fails or times out (2a):** Save/Load still calls `request_restore` with the advanced value held in memory, logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE`, sets `save_status` `FAILED`, and the worker retries the file with the next write job and after every later `WRITTEN` generation while memory is ahead of disk. A kill before then may replay that epoch once (OQ-25, an accepted and listed exposure: the device is failing and no write can fix that).
- **Missing or CRC-failing `slot_epoch.bin` (2b):** the value reads as `max(newest verified generation's header copy, 0) + 1`, logs `SL_EPOCH_FILE_REBUILT`, and is rewritten by the worker; a leftover `slot_epoch.tmp` is deleted (T-6). Deleting the side file by hand therefore re-keys the next stretch once, a tampering exposure of the same class as editing any save.

**3.5 Reaching the sim.** `request_restore` and `request_new_game(world_seed, restore_epoch = 0)` pass the epoch as an argument; the kernel range-checks it (`RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE`, domain 0 code 6) and exposes it read-only, sim-visible and **non-persisted, non-hashed** in the `kernel.clock` read view as `(T, world_seed, restore_epoch)` before the first `restore()`. The one derivation, `counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE * restore_epoch`, belongs to the kernel and ADR-0005 (`rng_derive_epoch`); Attention and Horror call it and never store the epoch (TR-attention-024, TR-horror-017). Determinism is defined given the pair: the same (save bytes, `restore_epoch`) replays identically, and tests pin the epoch. The phrase "excluded from the snapshot header" (TR-cmd-018) means *the kernel snapshot payload and every `H64`*: the **container** header carries the recovery copy of § 3.1, which is covered by the file trailer (file integrity) and by no state hash.

**3.6 Staging and hot copy.** Candidate selection (SL-8), the death-stub's one synchronous attempt per candidate and the newest and preceding **hot decoded copies** (SL-11) stand as written. The payload handed to `request_restore` is built in memory by Save/Load (not decoded from one blob): `Dictionary` of `StringName block_id -> {&"schema_version": int, &"data": Dictionary}`, with `kernel.clock` included, `data` dictionaries made read-only (`Dictionary.make_read_only()`; whether that is deep is **UNVERIFIED** and owners copy what they keep either way, OQ-53), and `expected_state_hash` the header `state_hash` as an `int`, or `null` when the file legitimately carries none (a release-build file that predates K-4: verdict `NONE`).

### Implementation Guidelines

Mandates are stated as must / must never so `/create-control-manifest` can extract them.

**Container and codec**
- Save/Load **must** write every block payload as `var_to_bytes(dictionary)` and decode only with `bytes_to_var`; it **must never** call `var_to_bytes_with_objects` or `bytes_to_var_with_objects`, and **must never** use a `Resource`, `.tres`, `.res`, `ResourceLoader` or `load()` for a save, a snapshot or a profile.
- The type walk **must** reject `TYPE_OBJECT` (including `EncodedObjectAsID`), `StringName`, every vector, rect, `Color`, `Callable`, `Signal`, `RID`, `NodePath` and non-finite floats; it **must** run on the worker in `VERIFYING` over the bytes just written and on the main thread (or hot-copy worker) after every load decode.
- 64-bit header fields **must** be read with `hex_decode()` and `decode_s64` / `decode_u64` after an exact-size check; code **must never** call `String.hex_to_int` or `int()`/`to_int()` on a 64-bit field, and **must never** parse a 64-bit or hash value from a JSON number. Header integers **must** be integral and strictly below 2^53.
- The trailer SHA-256 **must** be checked before the layout-id byte is judged, and `header_len` **must** be range-checked before any allocation.
- The file size **must** be checked against `MAX_SAVE_BYTES` before the file is read.
- Block data and the header **must never** contain a wall-clock value that the sim reads; `created_unix` is metadata.

**Write path and threading**
- A write **must** go to `gen_<write_epoch>_<k>.tmp`, flush, close, re-open, re-hash and decode before any rename; **every `store_*`, `flush` and rename result must be checked**; an existing generation **must never** be overwritten in place, renamed onto, or deleted before its successor verified; nothing **must** be written while the kernel is `FAULTED`.
- Only the Save/Load module **may** create a `Thread`; it **must** create one per job, **must** poll `is_alive()`, **must** call `wait_to_finish()` only on a thread that is not alive, and **must never** join a live thread, use `WorkerThreadPool`, `call_deferred` into Save/Load or the kernel, or hand the worker a `Node`, a block, a read view, a `Callable` that touches the scene tree, or a `Dictionary`.
- The main thread **must** drop its reference to a block's `PackedByteArray` at hand-off and **must never** mutate it afterwards.
- A due `slot_epoch.bin` write **must** be its own job, polled per frame; `request_restore` **must** be called only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`, or after the documented 2a failure path.
- Save & Quit **must** poll under `SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS` on the injected monotonic source and **must never** block the frame or join the worker; millisecond timeouts **must never** enter a gate input or a sim decision.
- The campaign lock **must** be a held `FileAccess` handle tested by a rename probe; it **must never** rely on an exclusive `FileAccess.open`.

**Blocks**
- A persisted block **must** register `snapshot`, `restore`, `default_state` and `post_restore` as ADR-0003 Callables, **must** declare `supported_versions`, `persist_scope` and `restore_after`, **must** return plain data (§ 1.2), and **must** copy restored contents into its existing block object; it **must never** call Save/Load, hold a file path, or replace its block object in `restore`.
- A restore failure **must** be reported with `ctx.fault(<OWNER>_RESTORE_*)`; a restore **must never** clamp an out-of-range value.
- A field that may exceed 2^53 **must** be declared `int64` in the owner's snapshot schema; a float **must never** stand in for an integer.
- Save/Load **must never** register a state block, a step hook, a command type, or `save_now` / `load(generation)` outside a dev build.

**Versioning**
- Save/Load **must never** rewrite a block's data and **must never** write a migrated payload back to an old file.
- The pre-check **must** refuse `catalogue_version` above the build's as INCOMPATIBLE without quarantining; `catalogue_hash` **must never** gate a load.
- Block versions **must** be read from `assets/data/saveload/block_versions.json` and cross-checked against the live registry before the first request; a mismatch **must** stop boot.
- The frozen golden save **must** never be regenerated; a change to the committed shapes' `registry_epoch` **must** arrive with a `schema_version` or `format_version` bump.

**Epoch**
- `restore_epoch` **must** be stored only in `slot_epoch.bin` (and as the read-only header copy), **must** never be inside a snapshot payload, an `H64` input or a block, and **must** reach the sim only as the `request_restore` / `request_new_game` argument and the `kernel.clock` view.
- An epoch advance **must** use `min(2^32 - 1, max(e_mem, e_slot) + 1)`; code **must never** decrease the epoch for a step-back, demotion, quarantine or a lost manifest.

## Alternatives Considered

### Alternative 1: Scripted binary writer with canonical TLV for storage and hashing (one encoding)
- **Description**: Store each block in ADR-0005's canonical TLV form and hash those same stored bytes, so file bytes are canonical and `payload_sha256` could double as a block hash.
- **Pros**: One encoding; byte-identical files for identical state; no dependence on `var_to_bytes` layout stability across engine versions.
- **Cons**: A scripted encoder and decoder for every field type on the capture path (the encode is main-thread time); every owner must express its snapshot as TLV before ADR-0005 is even Accepted; decode needs a hand-written bounded parser (more attack surface than the native decoder); no gain for integrity, which the SHA-256 chain already provides.
- **Rejection Reason**: Cost on the critical frame and a hard dependency on a sibling ADR for the sake of a property (byte-identical files) nothing needs: state equality is `state_hash`. Recorded as the **rejected-for-now** path: moving storage to canonical TLV later is a `format_version` bump with a container migration, and the per-block `snapshot()` contract does not change.

### Alternative 2: `Resource` / `ResourceSaver` (`.tres` or `.res`) saves
- **Description**: Snapshot blocks as `Resource` subclasses and save with `ResourceSaver`.
- **Pros**: Built-in versioning hooks, editor inspection, typed fields.
- **Cons**: A `.tres` can embed scripts and external resources, so a loaded save is a code-execution path; blocks are `RefCounted` plain data by registry stance; no trailer, no per-block hash, no ring control; scene-tree-adjacent loading.
- **Rejection Reason**: Violates the save-file trust model (SL-2) and registry `block_as_resource_or_node`.

### Alternative 3: JSON for the whole file (or base64 payloads inside JSON)
- **Description**: One JSON document; blocks as nested JSON or base64 strings.
- **Pros**: Human-readable, trivially diffable, one parser.
- **Cons**: JSON numbers arrive as `float` (probed: 2^53+1 corrupts silently), so every 64-bit or hashed value needs a string convention in every block; packed arrays become number lists (slow, large); base64 inflates by a third and costs main-thread time; no cheap partial verification.
- **Rejection Reason**: Fights S-1 in every block. JSON stays in the header and the dev dump, where its readability pays and its number typing is handled by § 1.3.

### Alternative 4: Single save file overwritten in place (or one file plus one backup)
- **Description**: One `save.sav`, rewritten each time, or a current and a previous file.
- **Pros**: Simplest; least disk.
- **Cons**: One bad write (or a crash mid-write, or a locked file) loses the campaign; two files cannot support the RISKY and fairness step-backs (SL-8), which need an older verified generation after a demotion; `AUTOSAVE_GENERATIONS` 1 is forbidden by invariant I4.
- **Rejection Reason**: Fails the "never overwrites a good save" requirement and the death-loop rules.

### Alternative 5: `WorkerThreadPool` tasks for the writer
- **Description**: Submit the write as a pool task and `wait_for_task_completion` when needed.
- **Pros**: No thread lifetime management; engine-scheduled.
- **Cons**: No timed wait and no way to abandon one task individually (training knowledge, **UNVERIFIED** on 4.7), so a join at the `DEAD` boundary or at quit could hang on a stuck disk; pool saturation by other users is outside this module's control.
- **Rejection Reason**: The design requires a job that can be abandoned and a main thread that never blocks. One `Thread` per job, polled, gives exactly that (probed).

### Alternative 6: Join the worker with a timeout (loop on a semaphore or a timed wait)
- **Description**: `Thread.wait_to_finish` after a timed `Semaphore` wait, bounded at quit.
- **Pros**: Familiar blocking shape.
- **Cons**: A blocking wait on the main thread at quit or at `DEAD` is a frame hang on a hung write; `Semaphore` has no timed wait in GDScript (training knowledge, **UNVERIFIED**); polling achieves the same bound without the hang.
- **Rejection Reason**: Polling under a monotonic timeout (§ 1.6) is bounded and never blocks.

### Alternative 7: Exclusive-open lock file, or process-id liveness for the single-instance guard
- **Description**: Create `campaign.lock` with an exclusive open (the GDD's wording), or store a process id and test it with `OS.is_process_running`.
- **Pros**: Conventional.
- **Cons**: `FileAccess.open` is not exclusive (probed: two WRITE opens succeed); `is_process_running` answers for the own process but whether it answers for a foreign non-child process is **UNVERIFIED**; a stale pid after a crash can mislead.
- **Rejection Reason**: The held-handle plus rename probe uses behaviour that was probed and releases itself when the holder dies (§ 1.7).

### Alternative 8: Keep `restore_epoch` in the generation header and rewrite it on restore (the original R1)
- **Description**: Persist the epoch inside the generation file and rewrite that file's header when a restore advances it.
- **Pros**: No side file.
- **Cons**: Rewriting a verified file changes its trailer and every key derived from it (SL-12's REBASED baseline), races the write protocol, and loses the value when that generation is quarantined or the ring steps back.
- **Rejection Reason**: Superseded by R14: the per-slot side file survives step-backs and a lost manifest and leaves every generation immutable after `VERIFYING`.

### Alternative 9: Split capture across frames to meet the 14.9 ms target (OQ-14)
- **Description**: Capture a few blocks per frame so no frame exceeds budget.
- **Pros**: No over-budget frame.
- **Cons**: The captured blocks would be from different ticks unless the sim freezes, which is what `SAVING` already does; a multi-frame capture breaks the kernel's atomic-`SAVING` rule and the single-`T` guarantee that `state_hash` and the reproduction compare rest on.
- **Rejection Reason**: Contradicts the kernel contract; kept only as mitigation rung 3, behind a kernel amendment, if the spike shows the single frame is visible.

## Consequences

### Positive
- A bad write, a locked target, a kill at any step or a corrupt newest file costs at most one interval; the ring and T-6 recovery make every partial state recoverable by rule, and the only file ever replaced is `campaign.json` or `slot_epoch.bin`, both rebuildable.
- One container and one payload form for WORLD and PROFILE: one decode path, one type walk, one fuzz target.
- 64-bit values are exact in the binary payload with no per-block convention, and the header's hex rule is mechanical and tested.
- The probe findings (objects slip through the encoder; `FileAccess` is not exclusive; `hex_to_int` saturates) are turned into mandatory checks before any code exists.
- The epoch survives kill, step-back and a lost manifest, is durable before the restore that uses it, and changes no generation file; quit buys no reroll.
- The main thread never blocks on I/O and never joins a live thread; quit is bounded by polling.

### Negative
- The type walk and the write-side decode are load-bearing, not belt-and-braces; a gap in either lets an object reach disk. Cost: a walk over up to 250 000 nodes at load (10 to 30 ms for a Graph-sized payload, F-8 estimate).
- Stored bytes are not canonical, so byte-comparing two saves proves nothing; tests must compare `state_hash`.
- One over-budget frame per autosave is accepted (§ 1.9) pending the spike.
- The lock protects only on Windows as probed; Linux and the Deck rely on single-instance launch.
- A hand-rolled CRC32 and a hand-rolled single-instance lock are code the project owns and must test.
- `var_to_bytes` byte layout stability across engine versions is training-knowledge-grade (**UNVERIFIED**); a Godot upgrade is a save-compatibility event for stored bytes and is covered by the golden fixture check.

## Risks
- **`flush` does not imply fsync, so a power cut can lose a "verified" generation.** Mitigation: the ring (at least two verified generations during any swap), T-6, and the bounded loss of one interval; SAVE-WRK-1 c records what the platform does.
- **Antivirus or an indexer holds the target (READ-held is only a proxy).** Mitigation: `RENAME_RETRY_COUNT`/`READ_RETRY_COUNT`, the `.bak` swap, the abandon-and-quarantine rule, and SAVE-WRK-1 a with Defender and OneDrive on.
- **Engine ERROR spam from `bytes_to_var` on hostile or fuzzed bytes (probed) trips gdUnit4 or warnings-as-errors.** Mitigation: decode only after hash checks; the fuzz suite mutates and re-hashes only in a dedicated test configuration that ADR-0010 must allow; recorded as a cross-ADR assumption.
- **A stray object, vector or `StringName` in a snapshot reaches disk.** Mitigation: the walk and the write-side decode (§ 1.2); a unit test per block that feeds a snapshot through encode, decode and walk.
- **Process exit prints a `~Thread` WARNING and an ObjectDB leak report (probed).** Mitigation: ADR-0010 allow-lists them for the quit path; an abandoned worker is the only source.
- **A worker blocked in a syscall rather than a sleep may keep the process alive at exit.** Mitigation: SAVE-WRK-1 d; if it does, Save & Quit reports `FAILED` and the player may force-quit; no data is at risk (the ring is intact).
- **The snapshot frame exceeds 14.9 ms by more than one frame, or on RM-DECK by a visible amount.** Mitigation: the rung ladder of § 1.9; the gate keeps the frame away from tells.
- **Registering fault domain 1 from a module that registers no block is outside ADR-0003's stated examples.** Mitigation: assumption recorded; ADR-0003's registrar already exposes `register_fault_domain` independent of blocks.
- **`min_reader_version` equals `format_version` so no older build ever opens a newer file.** Intentional for the MVP; the field exists so a later additive change can lower it.
- **`block_versions.json` and the live registry drift.** Mitigation: the boot cross-check refuses to start.
- **Typed-container and `PackedByteArray` round-trip beyond the probed cases** (nested typed containers, large arrays) is assumed from the probed behaviour. Mitigation: the per-block encode-decode-walk unit test.

## Performance Implications
- **CPU (main thread)**: Capture is the kernel's (`SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS` 16.7 ceiling). Save/Load adds `var_to_bytes` per block (synthetic: 32 blocks / 860 KB in 1.93 ms, dev machine) and a small hand-off, bounded by `SAVE_ENCODE_BUDGET_MS` 4 and `WRITE_HANDOFF_MAX_FRACTION` 0.05 as log thresholds, never truncating. Load adds header parse, `bytes_to_var` (synthetic 3.5 ms for 860 KB) and the type walk (10 to 30 ms for a Graph-sized payload, estimate). One over-budget frame per autosave is accepted pending SAVE-WRK-1 f (§ 1.9). Release-export numbers on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK are **pending the spike**; every figure above is probed 2026-10-28, synthetic.
- **CPU (worker)**: SHA-256 (0.7 ms at 300 KiB, 4.9 ms at 2 MiB, probed), file I/O (2 to 100 ms, AV adds 50 to 500, GDD estimates, UNVERIFIED), re-read and decode. None of it on the main thread.
- **Memory**: Two hot decoded generations (SL-11) at 100 to 300 KiB plus decoded overhead, measured by SAVE-WRK-2; the captured payload and encoded bytes live until hand-off; caps `MAX_SAVE_BYTES` 64 MiB and `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES` 32 MiB bound hostile input.
- **Load Time**: Estimate `restart_ms` 140 to 196 ms against the 1000 ms target (F-8), dominated by the 120 ms black hold; `t_epoch_wait` is one poll frame normally, up to 500 ms on a failing disk, and zero on a carried Continue.
- **Disk**: A typical generation 100 to 300 KiB, three positions plus temporaries, `profile.sav` and quarantine; `SAVE_SIZE_ALARM_BYTES` 2 MiB.
- **Network**: None.

## Validation Criteria
- **SAVE-WRK-1 a to h pass** on a Windows and a Linux/Deck `template_release` export (a, b, d and g with antivirus, OneDrive and a slow disk); the results are recorded in the ADR before acceptance.
- **Fault injection at every T-4 step and every T-6 row** (kill after each step) leaves a recoverable ring: after recovery the newest verified generation is never older than the one before the write started, and no file is lost that was not provably obsolete.
- **Pure pre-check fuzz:** `FUZZ_MUTATION_COUNT` 1000 byte mutations of a golden file never throw, never return a verdict outside the closed `SL_PRECHECK_*` set, never allocate by a corrupt length, and never reach the kernel; a separate re-hashed fuzz configuration (hashes recomputed after mutation) reaches decode and walk and is the only configuration that emits engine `ERROR` lines.
- **Walk tests:** a snapshot containing an `Object` (an `EncodedObjectAsID` after round trip), a `StringName`, a `Vector2i`, a `NaN`, a 17-deep nest and a 250 001-node array each fail `SL_PRECHECK_BLOCK_TYPE_FORBIDDEN` / `_DECODE_FAILED`; at write time the same snapshot ends `SL_WRITE_UNENCODABLE` with all previous generations intact.
- **64-bit tests:** `hex64` round trip over {0, 1, 2^53 - 1, 2^53, 2^53 + 1, 2^63 - 1, 2^63, 2^64 - 1}; a header JSON number at or above 2^53 is refused; a payload `int` of 2^53 + 7 round-trips through encode, decode and restore (`odometer`, TR-shipbody-007).
- **CRC32 vector:** `SlotEpoch.crc32("123456789")` equals `0xCBF43926`; a flipped bit in `slot_epoch.bin` takes the 2b path and logs `SL_EPOCH_FILE_REBUILT`.
- **Epoch tests (AC-SL-142, AC-SL-145):** death advances; Save & Quit then Continue of the newest `QUIT` generation carries and writes nothing; Continue of an `AUTO` generation advances; saturation at 2^32 - 1; a step-back and a deleted manifest never lower it; the same (save bytes, epoch) replays an identical state hash and a different epoch re-keys only threat draws; `request_restore` is never called before `EPOCH_DURABLE` except on the injected 2a path.
- **Thread tests:** a worker killed by an injected GDScript error is reaped as `SL_WRITE_WORKER_DIED` within one poll; an abandoned job's late generation lands in `quarantine/` as `STALE_EPOCH`; no live thread is ever joined (a lint test over the Save/Load module); `MAX_LIVE_ABANDONED_JOBS` is enforced.
- **Quit tests:** with an injected stalled worker, Save & Quit returns `FAILED` at `SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS` and the process exits on request without hanging.
- **Lock test (Windows):** a second process cannot rename a held `campaign.lock` and opens READ_ONLY; a crashed holder leaves no stale lock.
- **Hitch measurement (OQ-14):** the 14-block MVP slice's capture frame P99 on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK, release export, with the ratified `H64` capture-time hash; the ADR records whether rung 1 is needed.
- **Version tests:** a v1 golden loads; a stand-in with a bumped `schema_version` migrates through the owner chain and is not written back; a file whose `registry_epoch` differs and whose mandatory set fails is INCOMPATIBLE-dev and not quarantined; a `catalogue_version` above the build's is `SL_PRECHECK_CATALOGUE_NEWER` and not quarantined; the boot cross-check refuses a retired-but-registered block.
- **Zero-block test:** with Save/Load booted the registry holds exactly the kernel's own `kernel.clock` plus the registered game blocks and no Save/Load block or hook.

# ADR-0006: Save Container, Generations, Versioning and Restore Epoch

## Status
Proposed

## Date
2026-10-28

## Last Verified
2026-10-28 (against `design/gdd/save-load-and-versioned-format.md` SL-1 to SL-25, T-3 to T-6, F-5, F-8, F-9 and the Tuning Knobs tables; `docs/architecture/tr-baseline.md` rows citing ADR-0006; ADR-0001, ADR-0002 § 6, ADR-0003 §§ 3, 6, 9 and ADR-0007 § 3.4; `docs/engine-reference/godot/` `VERSION.md`, `breaking-changes.md`, `deprecated-apis.md`). The pinned engine reference has no core, file-I/O or threading module, so every engine claim here rests either on a probe run on the installed 4.7.2 editor on 2026-10-28 (marked **probed**) or on training knowledge (marked **UNVERIFIED**, with the spike that settles it). No game code exists. All probes were synthetic, headless, on a development machine with an editor binary; none is a release-export measurement.

## Decision Makers
Claude (author), running under `modes.automation: autonomous` (`project.yaml`); decisions logged for the user's review; the user has not yet reviewed this ADR. Engine-specialist and technical-director review: pending (joint review of ADR-0004 to ADR-0010 and this ADR). See Review Log.

## Summary
Sixty-five requirements from seventeen GDDs need a save file that is self-verifying, written without ever endangering a good generation, versioned from the first build, and paired with a per-slot `restore_epoch` that re-keys threat draws on death without letting quit or death be a reroll oracle. This ADR fixes one container (8-byte magic, JSON header, `var_to_bytes` block payloads, SHA-256 trailer), a ring of three generations written by one `Thread` per job that the main thread only polls, a two-level version scheme (container migrated by Save/Load, blocks by their owners), a PROFILE side file in the same container, and `slot_epoch.bin` made durable before every `request_restore`.

## Engine Compatibility

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (stable), GDScript |
| **Domain** | Core (file I/O, threading, serialisation, hashing) |
| **Knowledge Risk** | MEDIUM. The APIs used (`FileAccess`, `DirAccess`, `Thread`, `Mutex`, `HashingContext`, `var_to_bytes`, `bytes_to_var`, `JSON`, `PackedByteArray.encode_*`/`decode_*`, `hex_encode`/`hex_decode`) all predate 4.4, and `breaking-changes.md` lists only one relevant change (4.4: every `FileAccess.store_*` returns `bool`, sourced). But the reference has no module for them, so behaviour on Windows (rename, sharing, thread exit) is training knowledge unless probed here. The 4.7 typed-return override rule applies to the one `Callable` Save/Load registers (the control-outcome handler) and to nothing in the worker. |
| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`, `breaking-changes.md` (4.4 `FileAccess.store_*` row; 4.6 to 4.7 GDScript rows), `deprecated-apis.md` (no entry for the APIs used). No module file exists for this domain. |
| **Post-Cutoff APIs Used** | `FileAccess.store_*` returning `bool` (4.4; the whole write path depends on it). Typed `Dictionary[K, V]` (4.4) may appear inside snapshots; it survives the encoder (probed). Nothing from 4.5 to 4.7 is required. |
| **Probes run 2026-10-28 (4.7.2.stable.mono, Windows 11, headless, scratch directory outside the repo)** | (1) `DirAccess.rename` and `rename_absolute` over an existing, unlocked target: `OK`, target replaced, source gone. (2) Rename over a target held open by another `FileAccess` handle (READ or READ_WRITE): `ERR_FAILED` (1), target intact; rename of a source held open: `ERR_FAILED`; `remove_absolute` of a READ-held or WRITE-held file: `ERR_FAILED`. (3) `FileAccess.open(path, WRITE)` is **not exclusive**: a second WRITE open of the same path succeeded (and truncates); READ-open while WRITE-open succeeded; WRITE-open while READ-held succeeded. (4) `store_buffer`, `store_32` return `true`; `store_buffer` on a READ handle returns `false` with `get_error()` = 13 (`ERR_FILE_CANT_WRITE`); `get_buffer` past the end returns the available bytes and sets `eof_reached` and error 18. (5) `var_to_bytes` of an `int` above 2^53 (2^53+1) and of `PackedInt64Array` round-trips exactly; `Vector2i`, `StringName`, typed `Array[int]`, typed `Dictionary[String, int]`, `NaN` and `INF` all round-trip; **`var_to_bytes({"o": RefCounted.new()})` silently succeeds, encoding an `EncodedObjectAsID`, and `bytes_to_var` returns it as an `Object`**. (6) `bytes_to_var` of `var_to_bytes_with_objects` output returns `null` and logs an engine `ERROR` (`ERR_UNAUTHORIZED`); garbage and empty input return `null` and log an engine `ERROR`. (7) Two dictionaries with the same entries in different insertion order encode to **different** bytes. (8) `JSON.new().parse` returns every number as `float`; `9007199254740993` parses to `9007199254740992.0`. (9) `"ffffffffffffffff".hex_to_int()` logs an error and returns `INT64_MAX`; `String.hex_decode()` plus `PackedByteArray.decode_u64` / `decode_s64` is exact (a 64-bit pattern with the top bit set reads as a negative GDScript `int`, as expected). (10) `PackedByteArray` has **no** `crc32`; a 4-byte bitwise CRC32 in GDScript matched the standard check vector (`0xCBF43926` for `"123456789"`) and took about 1 microsecond per call. (12) `OS.is_process_running(OS.get_process_id())` is `true`. ## Context

### Problem Statement
The game's one failure consequence is death and restart from the last autosave (Pillar 5), and its horror depends on the player never being able to read the world through the save system (Pillars 1, 3, 4). That makes persistence unusually load-bearing: a bad write that costs a good generation destroys the campaign; a pause when the game saves tells the player a tell has closed; a restart that replays the identical threat draws makes death a free retry; a restart that lets quit choose the draws makes quit a reroll oracle; and a format that cannot be migrated strands every outside tester at the first schema change. The Save/Load GDD settles the behaviour and defers a dozen mechanism choices to "the atomic write, backup and thread model" ADR and to "the container ADR": what the bytes are, how a Windows rename is used safely, how a worker thread is owned, how a quit is waited for, how the 64-bit and JSON constraints are met, where `restore_epoch` lives and how it reaches the kernel, and whether the snapshot hitch is acceptable. Two probes (§ Engine Compatibility) also falsify two GDD sentences: `var_to_bytes` does encode objects, and `FileAccess.open` is not exclusive. Without one decision, each of the 14 persisted blocks would meet a slightly different container, and the first outside build would find the differences.

### Constraints
- **Save/Load registers zero state blocks and zero hooks** (SL-17, TR-saveload-018): ring bookkeeping must live outside the world, or it rolls back with a restore.
- **Exactly one thread boundary** exists (architecture § Data Flow 7): the save writer. `Thread`, `WorkerThreadPool` and `call_deferred` into kernel code are lint-forbidden elsewhere (CR-1a). The worker receives immutable `PackedByteArray`s, paths and integers only (TR-saveload-007).
- **Capture is synchronous inside the kernel's `SAVING` state** at a tick boundary (TR-cmd-017, TR-saveload-009); `SAVING` is atomic within one boundary service and never spans a frame (ADR-0003 § 9, ADR-0001 § 1).
- **A bad file never produces `FAULTED`** (TR-saveload-014): the pre-check is a pure function of `(bytes, registry view, build constants)` and runs before the kernel is touched.
- **Block objects are `RefCounted`, restore copies into the existing object** (registry `block_as_resource_or_node`; ADR-0003 § 2). No `Resource` or `.tres` path, ever (a script can ride in one).
- **Integer-only simulation** (ADR-0005 forward); JSON parses numbers as `float` (probed), so no 64-bit or hashed value may travel as a JSON number (S-1).
- **No wall clock in any sim decision** (kernel H9); millisecond I/O timeouts read an injected monotonic source and change no sim state (SL-23).
- **No autoload or static singleton** (registry `kernel_autoload_or_global`): Save/Load is constructed and injected by the composition root.
- **Fault codes** follow ADR-0003 § 6: `(DOMAIN_ID << 16) | local`, domain 1 = `save_load`, append-only.
- **Single player at MVP**; co-op replication, guest carry-over and Steam Auto-Cloud are later tiers and constrain only the path layout.

### Requirements
- One container format for WORLD generations and the PROFILE store, self-verifying by a trailer that lives outside the header.
- A write that never overwrites in place, never deletes a generation before its successor verified, never blocks the main thread, and never starts while the kernel is `FAULTED`.
- A load that classifies every failure (corrupt, incompatible, owner-failed, not-reproduced) and decides the next action from the class.
- Two-level versioning with an obligation to migrate that begins at the first outside build, and development saves that are refused rather than half-migrated.
- `restore_epoch` that survives a process kill, a lost manifest and a step-back, is durable before the restore that uses it, and reaches the sim only as an argument.
- A quit that waits for its write by polling, with a timeout, and never hangs the process on a stuck worker.
- A recorded ruling on the snapshot hitch (OQ-14) and a named spike for every engine claim the reference does not source.

## Decision

The decision has three parts, numbered so each can be reviewed on its own: **§ 1 the container and the write path**, **§ 2 versioning and migration**, **§ 3 the restore epoch**. Behaviour already fixed by the GDD (SL-1 to SL-25, T-3 to T-9, F-1 to F-10) is cited, not restated; this ADR decides what the GDD left as `[UNV]`, as an "ADR candidate", or wrong.

### Architecture Diagram
