gdd_sync.new: failure is reported through ctx.fault(<OWNER>_RESTORE_*) with the owner's domain code; Save/Load maps the kernel load_failed trigger to the RESTORE_FAILED class

gdd_sync.old: 64-bit values as two 32-bit halves or strings, never as JSON numbers
gdd_sync.new: halves or strings remain legal; native int64 is also accepted in the binary payload (exact); the convention is mandatory only where a value can reach JSON (header, dump-save)

gdd_sync.old: JSON-parsed integer-valued floats are accepted and re-cast to int
gdd_sync.new: binary payload ints are exact, so a float where an int is expected is a SHAPE failure; the re-cast clause applies only to dev JSON fixtures

gdd_sync.file: docs/architecture/architecture.md (Spikes that gate ADRs, Save worker row; Data Flow 6 and 7)
gdd_sync.old: Save worker (DirAccess.rename over an existing file on Windows ... snapshot hitch size)
gdd_sync.new: add the 2026-10-28 probe results and the SAVE-WRK-1 a to h checklist; note Save & Quit polls rather than joins; the quit-during-write bounded join is bounded polling

decisions.chosen: A single form: var_to_bytes(Dictionary) per block; a block that publishes canonical bytes embeds them as a PackedByteArray field. The GDD's second 'owner canonical byte form as raw bytes' container form is dropped.
decisions.reason: One decode path, one type walk, and a restore hand-off that is always a Dictionary matching ADR-0003's restore(data: Dictionary, ...); canonical TLV stays hash input only (ADR-0005). Reinterprets Graph LS-21 / TR-lsg-022, flagged for ADR-0011.

decisions.chosen: Two encodings by design: native var_to_bytes for storage, ADR-0005's canonical TLV for hash input; file bytes are not canonical. Canonical-TLV storage recorded as the rejected-for-now alternative (revisit as a format_version 2).
decisions.reason: Probed: insertion order changes var_to_bytes bytes; state equality is state_hash. Scripted TLV encoding on the capture path costs main-thread time and creates a hard dependency on a sibling ADR.

decisions.chosen: Do not trust the encoder. The type walk rejects TYPE_OBJECT (EncodedObjectAsID), StringName, vectors and non-finite floats; the worker decodes and walks what it just wrote (VERIFYING, SL_WRITE_UNENCODABLE).
decisions.reason: Probe: var_to_bytes silently encodes an Object as EncodedObjectAsID; SL-2's 'the form that does not encode objects' is wrong in the direction that matters.

decisions.point: Typed containers and Vector2i in snapshots
decisions.chosen: Typed Array[T] and Dictionary[K, V] are allowed; Vector2i, StringName and vectors remain banned by walk policy.
decisions.reason: Probed: typed containers, Vector2i and StringName all round-trip, so bans are enforcement, not encoder limits; settles SL-2's untyped-until-spike note.

decisions.chosen: Binary payloads accept native int64 (halves/strings remain legal); the strict-below-2^53 integral rule and string rendering apply to the JSON header and dump-save only; fields that may exceed 2^53 are declared int64 in the owner schema.
decisions.reason: Probed: var_to_bytes preserves 2^53+1 and PackedInt64Array exactly; the halves convention came from the JSON constraint. Affects TR-section-006, TR-assembly-013, TR-shipbody-007, TR-derelict-009, TR-sanity-020, TR-saveload-017.

decisions.chosen: String.hex_decode() + exact-size check + decode_s64/decode_u64; ban String.hex_to_int; header integers integral and strictly < 2^53.
decisions.reason: Probed: hex_to_int saturates to INT64_MAX with an engine error on 16 f's; JSON parses 2^53+1 to 2^53, which the strict bound catches.

decisions.chosen: Hand-rolled bitwise CRC32 (poly 0xEDB88320) over the 4 epoch bytes, 8-byte file (u32 LE + u32 LE CRC), unit-tested against 0xCBF43926.
decisions.reason: Probed: PackedByteArray has no crc32; the scripted loop matches the standard vector at about 1 microsecond; a truncated SHA-256 would change the GDD's 8-byte format for no gain.

decisions.chosen: Hold a FileAccess handle (READ suffices) on campaign.lock for the campaign lifetime; a second process rename-probes the file only when it exists (missing = not held); pid is diagnostic; no OS.is_process_running use.
decisions.reason: Probed: FileAccess WRITE-open is not exclusive, held files fail rename/remove with ERR_FAILED, a missing source also gives ERR_FAILED; handle dies with the process so no stale lock. Linux/Deck unverified, accepted exposure.

decisions.chosen: One Thread per WriteJob (RefCounted with Mutex-guarded status record), poll is_alive(), wait_to_finish only on a dead thread, never join a live one; WorkerThreadPool rejected; Thread exception scoped to the Save/Load module.
decisions.reason: Probed Thread.start/bind/is_alive/wait_to_finish behaviour; join and pool wait take no timeout (training knowledge, UNVERIFIED); abandonment semantics need an individually abandonable job.

decisions.chosen: Bounded polling under SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS 3000 on the monotonic source then request_shutdown; no join; late completion is just a QUIT generation; abandoned worker left to the OS and T-6.
decisions.reason: Probed: a live sleeping thread did not delay exit past 0.68 s (only a ~Thread WARNING and ObjectDB leak report); a worker blocked in a syscall is UNVERIFIED (SAVE-WRK-1 d).

decisions.chosen: Only for slot_epoch.bin and campaign.json (both recoverable by rule); generation swap keeps the .bak dance and never relies on rename-over.
decisions.reason: Probed: rename over an unlocked target works and a held target fails ERR_FAILED with the target intact; crash atomicity on NTFS UNVERIFIED; the .bak step makes every partial state recoverable (T-6).

decisions.point: Quarantine reason encoding and retired campaigns (GDD OQ-27)
decisions.chosen: Reason in the file name: quarantine/g<generation>_<REASON>_<k>.sav; retire_campaign renames the directory to user://saves_retired/<campaign_id>/.
decisions.reason: gen_next must read the generation from the name without opening the file; a sidecar or manifest entry can be lost separately from the file.

decisions.chosen: New pre-check refusal SL_PRECHECK_CATALOGUE_NEWER (INCOMPATIBLE, no quarantine) after step 12, before step 13, when header catalogue_version exceeds the build's; catalogue_hash never gates.
decisions.reason: Without it a downgrade surfaces as an owner-reported UNKNOWN_DEF failure that quarantines a good file after QUARANTINE_AFTER_FAILURES 2.

decisions.chosen: First 8 bytes of SHA-256 (HashingContext) over sorted 'block_id:schema_version:added_in_format' text lines, lowercase hex.
decisions.reason: Independent of ADR-0005's TLV/H64 and of the kernel, so the version-skew signal needs no sibling decision.

decisions.point: Where added_in_format, RETIRED_BLOCKS and the mandatory flag live
decisions.chosen: assets/data/saveload/block_versions.json loaded by the ADR-0007 pipeline, cross-checked against the live registry after the freeze by SaveBootCheck (domain-1 SL_BOOT_* codes); not added to BlockDescriptor.
decisions.reason: Leaves ADR-0003's descriptor field list unchanged; the check needs the live registry so it cannot live in ContentLoader.

decisions.point: OQ-14 snapshot hitch vs frame budget
decisions.chosen: Keep atomic SAVING, accept and document one over-budget frame per autosave (proposed; kernel owner to confirm); mitigation ladder only if SAVE-WRK-1 f shows it is visible: (1) skip snapshot() for unchanged blocks via cached hashes, (2) encode on the worker with a private deep copy, (3) split capture with a kernel amendment.
decisions.reason: Probed synthetic evidence: encode 1.9 ms, deep copy 2.0 ms, SHA-256 0.7 ms at 300 KiB, decode 3.5 ms, so the Save/Load-owned share is of order 1 to 2 ms; the unmeasured share is owners' snapshot() and the capture-time H64 hash; splitting capture contradicts the kernel's atomic-SAVING rule.

decisions.chosen: SaveLoadFaults (DOMAIN_ID 1) packs the closed SL_PRECHECK_/WRITE_/LOAD_/VERIFY_/EPOCH_/QUIT_/NEW_GAME_/BOOT_ sets and is registered via register_fault_domain so diagnostics print save_load.NAME; none faults the kernel. Knob range/invariant failures are domain-2 ScalarTable errors (ADR-0007).
decisions.reason: Registering a domain is neither a block nor a hook so TR-saveload-018 holds; a bad file is a value, never FAULTED; respects ADR-0007's forbidden foreign_boot_code pattern.

decisions.chosen: SaveService (RefCounted, no scene tree) driven by SaveHost (Node, PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS, priority 0, after TICK_DRIVER); a control-plane caller with a limited read facet, not a subscriber; uses set_outcome_handler for the snapshot payload and K-4 verdict.
decisions.reason: Keeps observation after the driver's boundary service in the same frame; no new subscriber class; PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS frame polling in PAUSED/LOADING is UNVERIFIED (SAVE-WRK-1 e).

decisions.point: Staged restore payload shape and expected_state_hash
decisions.chosen: Dictionary of StringName block_id -> {schema_version: int, data: Dictionary} built in memory (never decoded from one blob), data read-only; expected_state_hash is the header state_hash as int, or null for a legitimate NONE verdict; StringName keys never enter a file (header block ids are Strings).
decisions.reason: Matches ADR-0002's registered request_restore signature and the block_as_resource_or_node stance; nullable type is raised as an open question for ADR-0002.

decisions.point: Restore rule wording across owner GDDs
decisions.chosen: Single rule: validate into scratch, then copy contents into the existing block object; failure only via ctx.fault(<OWNER>_RESTORE_*), never a return tuple, never clamp.
decisions.reason: Reconciles 'whole-block replace' / 'swaps whole tables' and '(ok, reason, detail)' in owner GDDs with registry block_as_resource_or_node and ADR-0003's CompletionToken contract (the latter is ADR-0003's sync).

decisions.chosen: profile.sav in the same container (file_kind PROFILE, no state_hash, no restore_epoch), ring of one plus a permanent .bak, written on per-block hash change (ADR-0005 cached hashes), on QUIT, with PROFILE_MIN_WRITE_GAP_TICKS 300; zero PROFILE blocks at MVP, mechanism tested with a synthetic block.
decisions.reason: SL-9 plus the swap keeping the .bak instead of deleting it; PROFILE survives in-session restores because only WORLD blocks are passed to request_restore.

decisions.chosen: slot_epoch.bin is its own worker job, never queued behind a generation write, polled once per frame by SaveHost; request_restore only after EPOCH_DURABLE or the logged SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE 2a path (RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS 500).
decisions.reason: R14: kernel LOADING stays atomic and holds no wait on Save/Load I/O; a failing device cannot block the restore.

decisions.point: Header copy vs 'excluded from the snapshot header' (TR-cmd-018)
decisions.chosen: The container header keeps a read-only write-time restore_epoch copy used only for the 2b rebuild rule; it is covered by the file trailer and by no state hash; 'snapshot header' is read as the kernel snapshot payload.
decisions.reason: Reconciles SL-1/SL-23 with TR-cmd-018 and IC-5 without making the epoch a hashed or persisted block field.

cross_adr_assumptions.assumption: Save/Load is a control-plane caller with a limited read facet (kernel.clock, controller.state loco_state, graph failures, attention.view, suit vitals_state, Assembly/Interaction pure reads), not one of the subscriber classes; PROFILE-change detection and the RISKY/event gates use tick-boundary polls and cached block hashes, not subscriptions. Mitigation rung 1 (skip snapshot() for unchanged blocks) additionally needs ADR-0004's debug-build check that every changed block marked a dirty key. If ADR-0004 prefers a control-plane end-of-tick callback instead of the SaveHost priority-0 frame poll, SL-13's provisional channel is replaced (OQ-F).

hash_algo 2 = H64 (first 8 bytes of SHA-256 via HashingContext, little-endian, ratified by the GDD); canonical TLV is hash input only and never the stored form; per-block cached hashes are available to Save/Load for the PROFILE diff and block_state_hash and to mitigation rung 1; the kernel can compute state_hash(PERSIST, T) during LOADING for K-4; rng_derive_epoch with RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE derives threat draws from restore_epoch and restore_epoch is never an H64 input; ADR-0005 and the kernel state the read-only kernel.clock copy once (IC-5).

One scoped Thread exception and one FileAccess/DirAccess exception for the Save/Load module (everything else keeps Thread, WorkerThreadPool and call_deferred forbidden); the lint flags var_to_bytes_with_objects, hex_to_int on 64-bit fields and join-on-live-thread patterns; gdUnit4 and warnings-as-errors tolerate the engine ERROR lines bytes_to_var prints on hostile bytes in the dedicated re-hashed fuzz configuration and the ~Thread WARNING plus ObjectDB leak report at exit with an abandoned worker; the scripted CRC32 lives in src under the module; the saved-bytes type walk is a runtime check, not a lint.

BlockDescriptor already carries supported_versions, persist_scope and restore_after (added_in_format and the mandatory flag are deliberately not added); restore failure is reported via ctx.fault with the owner's domain code and the kernel's load_failed trigger reaches Save/Load through the ControlOutcome; register_fault_domain may be called by a module that registers no block or hook (Save/Load, domain 1); SAVING remains atomic within one boundary service; restore copies contents into the existing block object; the restore data parameter is a Dictionary.

request_snapshot's ControlOutcome delivers the captured payload as a caller-owned deep copy and request_restore's outcome carries the K-4 verdict {T, computed_hash, match}; request_restore's payload is a Dictionary of StringName block_id -> {schema_version, data}; expected_state_hash is nullable (Variant or typed optional) so a legitimate NONE verdict can be expressed; request_restore and request_new_game range-check restore_epoch to u32 via kernel code RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE.

The boundary service serves control-plane requests in arrival order at the next boundary and clears the accumulator on every transition into RUNNING; SaveHost polls at the engine-default priority 0 after TICK_DRIVER -50 so its observations follow the driver in the same frame; the KernelHost PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS pattern also holds for SaveHost in PAUSED/LOADING (UNVERIFIED, SAVE-WRK-1 e).

Save/Load's tuning knobs load as a ScalarTable under assets/data/saveload/ with its range checks and structural invariants (I1 to I13, TR-saveload-024) raised as domain-2 errors by the ADR-0007 machinery; assets/data/saveload/block_versions.json (added_in_format, RETIRED_BLOCKS, mandatory flags) is a closed-schema manifest-listed table; catalogue_version is a plain int from the Item DB meta.json handed to the composition root as a build constant and ADR-0007's alias path resolves renamed defs for older catalogues.

The Graph embeds its canonical_bytes() as a PackedByteArray field of its snapshot dictionary instead of a separate container byte form; this reinterprets LS-21 / TR-lsg-022 ('never var_to_bytes for saves' becomes 'never var_to_bytes bytes as hash input') and needs the Graph owner's confirmation; graph.state stays under MAX_BLOCK_BYTES and the walk's 250000-node bound.

Consumes the staged restore payload shape of ADR-0006 section 3.6 (StringName block_id -> {schema_version, data}) and orders restores by restore_after; the two-phase rule is 'validate into scratch, copy contents in place'.

SaveHost at priority 0 is a control-plane host, not a presentation subscriber, and the Presenter holds the down sheet's last frame during the DEAD-to-request_restore staging interval (at most RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS) without any presentation write to the simulation.

open_questions: OQ-A: The OQ-14 ruling (keep atomic SAVING, accept one over-budget frame per autosave) is proposed under autonomous mode and needs the kernel owner's agreement; if SAVE-WRK-1 f shows the frame is visible, rung 1 needs ADR-0004 and ADR-0005 Accepted, rung 3 a kernel GDD amendment.
OQ-B: Type of expected_state_hash in request_restore: null expresses 'no verdict' (a pre-K-4 release file); ADR-0002 registered the signature without a type (should be Variant or a typed optional).
OQ-C: Whether Dictionary.make_read_only() is deep for the staged payload is UNVERIFIED; owners copy what they keep either way (OQ-53 a).

OQ-D: Single-instance protection on Linux/Steam Deck is absent by design (rename of an open file is expected to succeed there, UNVERIFIED); decide at Alpha whether a second mechanism is worth the code.
OQ-E: Whether to move storage to canonical TLV (rejected-for-now Alternative 1) as a format_version 2 once ADR-0005 is Accepted and the Graph's canonical_bytes() exists.

OQ-F: Whether SaveHost's frame poll at priority 0 gives the right 'tick boundary' semantics for the observation set, or ADR-0004 should offer a control-plane end-of-tick callback (SL-13's provisional channel).
OQ-G: How ADR-0010's lint and gdUnit4/warnings-as-errors configuration tolerate bytes_to_var engine ERROR lines (re-hashed fuzz configuration) and the ~Thread exit WARNING.
OQ-H: Co-op: whether a guest's reserved saveload.request_save command and a guest-side restore_epoch view need a separate carrier (ADR-0032).
OQ-I: Dropping the container's second payload form reinterprets the Graph's LS-21 / TR-lsg-022 rule; ADR-0011 and the Graph owner must confirm the Graph embeds canonical_bytes() as a snapshot field.

SAVE-WRK-1 (gates acceptance) is still to run: antivirus/indexer-held rename targets, crash atomicity of the swap at every T-4 step, flush vs fsync, quit with a worker blocked in a syscall, PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS polling in PAUSED/SAVING/LOADING, the real snapshot hitch on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK, the campaign.lock on Linux/Deck, and Mutex status-record race behaviour; all probes in the ADR (2026-10-28) are synthetic, headless, editor-binary results.

Two probe artefacts remain outside the repo: scratch scripts in C:/Users/dasbl/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/adr-probes/0006/ and a leftover folder under C:/Users/dasbl/AppData/Roaming/Godot/app_userdata/[unnamed project]/adr0006probe (an rm was denied); neither is in the repository.

Conflict surfaced against no registry stance: the ADR does not contradict architecture.yaml, but it reinterprets three GDD/TR wordings (TR-lsg-022 'never var_to_bytes', TR-cmd-018 'excluded from the snapshot header', TR-suit-009 'StringName keys') listed in gdd_sync; the orchestrator should confirm these with the owning ADRs.

data.summary: ADR-0006 fixes the save container (8-byte magic, JSON header, one var_to_bytes payload form per block, SHA-256 trailer), a 3-generation ring written by one polled Thread per job with a never-overwrite swap, two-level versioning (container by Save/Load, blocks by owners via ctx.fault), a PROFILE side file, and slot_epoch.bin (u32 + hand-rolled CRC32) made durable before every request_restore. It records the 2026-10-28 probes on 4.7.2 that falsify two GDD sentences (var_to_bytes encodes objects as EncodedObjectAsID; FileAccess WRITE-open is not exclusive), rules on OQ-14 (keep atomic SAVING, accept one over-budget frame per autosave, with a three-rung mitigation ladder), and gates acceptance on the SAVE-WRK-1 spike; all 65 TR rows citing ADR-0006 are covered (41 in the main tables, 24 owner-obligation rows in the owned-elsewhere table).

gdd_sync.new: var_to_bytes DOES encode an Object, as an EncodedObjectAsID (probed 2026-10-28); the defence is the bounded type walk rejecting TYPE_OBJECT plus the write-side VERIFYING decode and walk, not the encoder

gdd_sync.old: `snapshot()` uses untyped containers until the spike resolves typed-container encoding [UNV]
gdd_sync.new: typed Array[T] and Dictionary[K, V] survive var_to_bytes / bytes_to_var (probed); snapshots may use typed or untyped containers and the walk checks decoded element types

gdd_sync.old: or the owner's own canonical byte form where it publishes one (the Graph's `canonical_bytes()`, LS-21), as raw bytes inside the container
gdd_sync.new: a block that publishes canonical bytes embeds them as a PackedByteArray field of its snapshot Dictionary; one payload form, canonical bytes are hash input only (ADR-0005)

gdd_sync.old: numeric values below 2^53 (S-1) for every block payload
gdd_sync.new: payload ints may be native int64 (var_to_bytes is exact, probed with 2^53+1); the strict-below-2^53 rule and the string convention apply to the JSON header and dump-save; a field that may reach 2^53 is declared int64 in the owner schema; two 32-bit halves remain legal

gdd_sync.old: hex decoding is exact-width ... no general string-to-int parse
gdd_sync.new: add the mechanism: String.hex_decode() + exact-size check + decode_s64 / decode_u64; String.hex_to_int is banned (saturates to INT64_MAX with an engine error, probed)

decisions.chosen: A single form: var_to_bytes(Dictionary) per block; a block that publishes canonical bytes embeds them as a PackedByteArray field. The GDD's second 'owner canonical byte form as raw bytes' container form is dropped.
decisions.reason: One decode path, one type walk, and a restore hand-off that is always a Dictionary matching ADR-0003's restore(data: Dictionary, ...); canonical TLV stays hash input only (ADR-0005). Reinterprets Graph LS-21 / TR-lsg-022, flagged for ADR-0011.

decisions.chosen: Two encodings by design: native var_to_bytes for storage, ADR-0005's canonical TLV for hash input; file bytes are not canonical. Canonical-TLV storage recorded as the rejected-for-now alternative (revisit as a format_version 2).
decisions.reason: Probed: insertion order changes var_to_bytes bytes; state equality is state_hash. Scripted TLV encoding on the capture path costs main-thread time and creates a hard dependency on a sibling ADR.

decisions.chosen: Do not trust the encoder. The type walk rejects TYPE_OBJECT (EncodedObjectAsID), StringName, vectors and non-finite floats; the worker decodes and walks what it just wrote (VERIFYING, SL_WRITE_UNENCODABLE).
decisions.reason: Probe: var_to_bytes silently encodes an Object as EncodedObjectAsID; SL-2's 'the form that does not encode objects' is wrong in the direction that matters.

decisions.point: Typed containers and Vector2i in snapshots
decisions.chosen: Typed Array[T] and Dictionary[K, V] are allowed; Vector2i, StringName and vectors remain banned by walk policy.
decisions.reason: Probed: typed containers, Vector2i and StringName all round-trip, so bans are enforcement, not encoder limits; settles SL-2's untyped-until-spike note.

decisions.chosen: Binary payloads accept native int64 (halves/strings remain legal); the strict-below-2^53 integral rule and string rendering apply to the JSON header and dump-save only; fields that may exceed 2^53 are declared int64 in the owner schema.
decisions.reason: Probed: var_to_bytes preserves 2^53+1 and PackedInt64Array exactly; the halves convention came from the JSON constraint. Affects TR-section-006, TR-assembly-013, TR-shipbody-007, TR-derelict-009, TR-sanity-020, TR-saveload-017.

decisions.chosen: String.hex_decode() + exact-size check + decode_s64/decode_u64; ban String.hex_to_int; header integers integral and strictly < 2^53.
decisions.reason: Probed: hex_to_int saturates to INT64_MAX with an engine error on 16 f's; JSON parses 2^53+1 to 2^53, which the strict bound catches.

decisions.chosen: Hand-rolled bitwise CRC32 (poly 0xEDB88320) over the 4 epoch bytes, 8-byte file (u32 LE + u32 LE CRC), unit-tested against 0xCBF43926.
decisions.reason: Probed: PackedByteArray has no crc32; the scripted loop matches the standard vector at about 1 microsecond; a truncated SHA-256 would change the GDD's 8-byte format for no gain.

decisions.chosen: Hold a FileAccess handle (READ suffices) on campaign.lock for the campaign lifetime; a second process rename-probes the file only when it exists (missing = not held); pid is diagnostic; no OS.is_process_running use.
decisions.reason: Probed: FileAccess WRITE-open is not exclusive, held files fail rename/remove with ERR_FAILED, a missing source also gives ERR_FAILED; handle dies with the process so no stale lock. Linux/Deck unverified, accepted exposure.

decisions.chosen: One Thread per WriteJob (RefCounted with Mutex-guarded status record), poll is_alive(), wait_to_finish only on a dead thread, never join a live one; WorkerThreadPool rejected; Thread exception scoped to the Save/Load module.
decisions.reason: Probed Thread.start/bind/is_alive/wait_to_finish behaviour; join and pool wait take no timeout (training knowledge, UNVERIFIED); abandonment semantics need an individually abandonable job.

decisions.chosen: Bounded polling under SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS 3000 on the monotonic source then request_shutdown; no join; late completion is just a QUIT generation; abandoned worker left to the OS and T-6.
decisions.reason: Probed: a live sleeping thread did not delay exit past 0.68 s (only a ~Thread WARNING and ObjectDB leak report); a worker blocked in a syscall is UNVERIFIED (SAVE-WRK-1 d).

decisions.chosen: Only for slot_epoch.bin and campaign.json (both recoverable by rule); generation swap keeps the .bak dance and never relies on rename-over.
decisions.reason: Probed: rename over an unlocked target works and a held target fails ERR_FAILED with the target intact; crash atomicity on NTFS UNVERIFIED; the .bak step makes every partial state recoverable (T-6).

decisions.point: Quarantine reason encoding and retired campaigns (GDD OQ-27)
decisions.chosen: Reason in the file name: quarantine/g<generation>_<REASON>_<k>.sav; retire_campaign renames the directory to user://saves_retired/<campaign_id>/.
decisions.reason: gen_next must read the generation from the name without opening the file; a sidecar or manifest entry can be lost separately from the file.

decisions.chosen: New pre-check refusal SL_PRECHECK_CATALOGUE_NEWER (INCOMPATIBLE, no quarantine) after step 12, before step 13, when header catalogue_version exceeds the build's; catalogue_hash never gates.
decisions.reason: Without it a downgrade surfaces as an owner-reported UNKNOWN_DEF failure that quarantines a good file after QUARANTINE_AFTER_FAILURES 2.

decisions.chosen: First 8 bytes of SHA-256 (HashingContext) over sorted 'block_id:schema_version:added_in_format' text lines, lowercase hex.
decisions.reason: Independent of ADR-0005's TLV/H64 and of the kernel, so the version-skew signal needs no sibling decision.

decisions.point: Where added_in_format, RETIRED_BLOCKS and the mandatory flag live
decisions.chosen: assets/data/saveload/block_versions.json loaded by the ADR-0007 pipeline, cross-checked against the live registry after the freeze by SaveBootCheck (domain-1 SL_BOOT_* codes); not added to BlockDescriptor.
decisions.reason: Leaves ADR-0003's descriptor field list unchanged; the check needs the live registry so it cannot live in ContentLoader.

decisions.point: OQ-14 snapshot hitch vs frame budget
decisions.chosen: Keep atomic SAVING, accept and document one over-budget frame per autosave (proposed; kernel owner to confirm); mitigation ladder only if SAVE-WRK-1 f shows it is visible: (1) skip snapshot() for unchanged blocks via cached hashes, (2) encode on the worker with a private deep copy, (3) split capture with a kernel amendment.
decisions.reason: Probed synthetic evidence: encode 1.9 ms, deep copy 2.0 ms, SHA-256 0.7 ms at 300 KiB, decode 3.5 ms, so the Save/Load-owned share is of order 1 to 2 ms; the unmeasured share is owners' snapshot() and the capture-time H64 hash; splitting capture contradicts the kernel's atomic-SAVING rule.

decisions.chosen: SaveLoadFaults (DOMAIN_ID 1) packs the closed SL_PRECHECK_/WRITE_/LOAD_/VERIFY_/EPOCH_/QUIT_/NEW_GAME_/BOOT_ sets and is registered via register_fault_domain so diagnostics print save_load.NAME; none faults the kernel. Knob range/invariant failures are domain-2 ScalarTable errors (ADR-0007).
decisions.reason: Registering a domain is neither a block nor a hook so TR-saveload-018 holds; a bad file is a value, never FAULTED; respects ADR-0007's forbidden foreign_boot_code pattern.

decisions.chosen: SaveService (RefCounted, no scene tree) driven by SaveHost (Node, PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS, priority 0, after TICK_DRIVER); a control-plane caller with a limited read facet, not a subscriber; uses set_outcome_handler for the snapshot payload and K-4 verdict.
decisions.reason: Keeps observation after the driver's boundary service in the same frame; no new subscriber class; PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS frame polling in PAUSED/LOADING is UNVERIFIED (SAVE-WRK-1 e).

decisions.point: Staged restore payload shape and expected_state_hash
decisions.chosen: Dictionary of StringName block_id -> {schema_version: int, data: Dictionary} built in memory (never decoded from one blob), data read-only; expected_state_hash is the header state_hash as int, or null for a legitimate NONE verdict; StringName keys never enter a file (header block ids are Strings).
decisions.reason: Matches ADR-0002's registered request_restore signature and the block_as_resource_or_node stance; nullable type is raised as an open question for ADR-0002.

decisions.point: Restore rule wording across owner GDDs
decisions.chosen: Single rule: validate into scratch, then copy contents into the existing block object; failure only via ctx.fault(<OWNER>_RESTORE_*), never a return tuple, never clamp.
decisions.reason: Reconciles 'whole-block replace' / 'swaps whole tables' and '(ok, reason, detail)' in owner GDDs with registry block_as_resource_or_node and ADR-0003's CompletionToken contract (the latter is ADR-0003's sync).

decisions.chosen: profile.sav in the same container (file_kind PROFILE, no state_hash, no restore_epoch), ring of one plus a permanent .bak, written on per-block hash change (ADR-0005 cached hashes), on QUIT, with PROFILE_MIN_WRITE_GAP_TICKS 300; zero PROFILE blocks at MVP, mechanism tested with a synthetic block.
decisions.reason: SL-9 plus the swap keeping the .bak instead of deleting it; PROFILE survives in-session restores because only WORLD blocks are passed to request_restore.

decisions.chosen: slot_epoch.bin is its own worker job, never queued behind a generation write, polled once per frame by SaveHost; request_restore only after EPOCH_DURABLE or the logged SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE 2a path (RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS 500).
decisions.reason: R14: kernel LOADING stays atomic and holds no wait on Save/Load I/O; a failing device cannot block the restore.

decisions.point: Header copy vs 'excluded from the snapshot header' (TR-cmd-018)
decisions.chosen: The container header keeps a read-only write-time restore_epoch copy used only for the 2b rebuild rule; it is covered by the file trailer and by no state hash; 'snapshot header' is read as the kernel snapshot payload.
decisions.reason: Reconciles SL-1/SL-23 with TR-cmd-018 and IC-5 without making the epoch a hashed or persisted block field.

cross_adr_assumptions.assumption: Save/Load is a control-plane caller with a limited read facet (kernel.clock, controller.state loco_state, graph failures, attention.view, suit vitals_state, Assembly/Interaction pure reads), not one of the subscriber classes; PROFILE-change detection and the RISKY/event gates use tick-boundary polls and cached block hashes, not subscriptions. Mitigation rung 1 (skip snapshot() for unchanged blocks) additionally needs ADR-0004's debug-build check that every changed block marked a dirty key. If ADR-0004 prefers a control-plane end-of-tick callback instead of the SaveHost priority-0 frame poll, SL-13's provisional channel is replaced (OQ-F).

hash_algo 2 = H64 (first 8 bytes of SHA-256 via HashingContext, little-endian, ratified by the GDD); canonical TLV is hash input only and never the stored form; per-block cached hashes are available to Save/Load for the PROFILE diff and block_state_hash and to mitigation rung 1; the kernel can compute state_hash(PERSIST, T) during LOADING for K-4; rng_derive_epoch with RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE derives threat draws from restore_epoch and restore_epoch is never an H64 input; ADR-0005 and the kernel state the read-only kernel.clock copy once (IC-5).

One scoped Thread exception and one FileAccess/DirAccess exception for the Save/Load module (everything else keeps Thread, WorkerThreadPool and call_deferred forbidden); the lint flags var_to_bytes_with_objects, hex_to_int on 64-bit fields and join-on-live-thread patterns; gdUnit4 and warnings-as-errors tolerate the engine ERROR lines bytes_to_var prints on hostile bytes in the dedicated re-hashed fuzz configuration and the ~Thread WARNING plus ObjectDB leak report at exit with an abandoned worker; the scripted CRC32 lives in src under the module; the saved-bytes type walk is a runtime check, not a lint.

BlockDescriptor already carries supported_versions, persist_scope and restore_after (added_in_format and the mandatory flag are deliberately not added); restore failure is reported via ctx.fault with the owner's domain code and the kernel's load_failed trigger reaches Save/Load through the ControlOutcome; register_fault_domain may be called by a module that registers no block or hook (Save/Load, domain 1); SAVING remains atomic within one boundary service; restore copies contents into the existing block object; the restore data parameter is a Dictionary.

request_snapshot's ControlOutcome delivers the captured payload as a caller-owned deep copy and request_restore's outcome carries the K-4 verdict {T, computed_hash, match}; request_restore's payload is a Dictionary of StringName block_id -> {schema_version, data}; expected_state_hash is nullable (Variant or typed optional) so a legitimate NONE verdict can be expressed; request_restore and request_new_game range-check restore_epoch to u32 via kernel code RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE.

The boundary service serves control-plane requests in arrival order at the next boundary and clears the accumulator on every transition into RUNNING; SaveHost polls at the engine-default priority 0 after TICK_DRIVER -50 so its observations follow the driver in the same frame; the KernelHost PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS pattern also holds for SaveHost in PAUSED/LOADING (UNVERIFIED, SAVE-WRK-1 e).

Save/Load's tuning knobs load as a ScalarTable under assets/data/saveload/ with its range checks and structural invariants (I1 to I13, TR-saveload-024) raised as domain-2 errors by the ADR-0007 machinery; assets/data/saveload/block_versions.json (added_in_format, RETIRED_BLOCKS, mandatory flags) is a closed-schema manifest-listed table; catalogue_version is a plain int from the Item DB meta.json handed to the composition root as a build constant and ADR-0007's alias path resolves renamed defs for older catalogues.

The Graph embeds its canonical_bytes() as a PackedByteArray field of its snapshot dictionary instead of a separate container byte form; this reinterprets LS-21 / TR-lsg-022 ('never var_to_bytes for saves' becomes 'never var_to_bytes bytes as hash input') and needs the Graph owner's confirmation; graph.state stays under MAX_BLOCK_BYTES and the walk's 250000-node bound.

Consumes the staged restore payload shape of ADR-0006 section 3.6 (StringName block_id -> {schema_version, data}) and orders restores by restore_after; the two-phase rule is 'validate into scratch, copy contents in place'.

SaveHost at priority 0 is a control-plane host, not a presentation subscriber, and the Presenter holds the down sheet's last frame during the DEAD-to-request_restore staging interval (at most RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS) without any presentation write to the simulation.

open_questions: OQ-A: The OQ-14 ruling (keep atomic SAVING, accept one over-budget frame per autosave) is proposed under autonomous mode and needs the kernel owner's agreement; if SAVE-WRK-1 f shows the frame is visible, rung 1 needs ADR-0004 and ADR-0005 Accepted, rung 3 a kernel GDD amendment.
OQ-B: Type of expected_state_hash in request_restore: null expresses 'no verdict' (a pre-K-4 release file); ADR-0002 registered the signature without a type (should be Variant or a typed optional).
OQ-C: Whether Dictionary.make_read_only() is deep for the staged payload is UNVERIFIED; owners copy what they keep either way (OQ-53 a).

OQ-D: Single-instance protection on Linux/Steam Deck is absent by design (rename of an open file is expected to succeed there, UNVERIFIED); decide at Alpha whether a second mechanism is worth the code.
OQ-E: Whether to move storage to canonical TLV (rejected-for-now Alternative 1) as a format_version 2 once ADR-0005 is Accepted and the Graph's canonical_bytes() exists.

OQ-F: Whether SaveHost's frame poll at priority 0 gives the right 'tick boundary' semantics for the observation set, or ADR-0004 should offer a control-plane end-of-tick callback (SL-13's provisional channel).
OQ-G: How ADR-0010's lint and gdUnit4/warnings-as-errors configuration tolerate bytes_to_var engine ERROR lines (re-hashed fuzz configuration) and the ~Thread exit WARNING.
OQ-H: Co-op: whether a guest's reserved saveload.request_save command and a guest-side restore_epoch view need a separate carrier (ADR-0032).
OQ-I: Dropping the container's second payload form reinterprets the Graph's LS-21 / TR-lsg-022 rule; ADR-0011 and the Graph owner must confirm the Graph embeds canonical_bytes() as a snapshot field.

SAVE-WRK-1 (gates acceptance) is still to run: antivirus/indexer-held rename targets, crash atomicity of the swap at every T-4 step, flush vs fsync, quit with a worker blocked in a syscall, PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS polling in PAUSED/SAVING/LOADING, the real snapshot hitch on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK, the campaign.lock on Linux/Deck, and Mutex status-record race behaviour; all probes in the ADR (2026-10-28) are synthetic, headless, editor-binary results.

Two probe artefacts remain outside the repo: scratch scripts in C:/Users/dasbl/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/adr-probes/0006/ and a leftover folder under C:/Users/dasbl/AppData/Roaming/Godot/app_userdata/[unnamed project]/adr0006probe (an rm was denied); neither is in the repository.

Conflict surfaced against no registry stance: the ADR does not contradict architecture.yaml, but it reinterprets three GDD/TR wordings (TR-lsg-022 'never var_to_bytes', TR-cmd-018 'excluded from the snapshot header', TR-suit-009 'StringName keys') listed in gdd_sync; the orchestrator should confirm these with the owning ADRs.
